Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Compensation Committee and adopted by Board resolution; re-approved at the Q1 committee meeting each year and on any amendment to the exchange listing standard.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Policy filed as Exhibit 97 to every Form 10-K and both clawback check-boxes completed on the 10-K cover page, due 60/75/90 days after fiscal year end by filer status; any recovery action disclosed in the Item 402(w) narrative of the next annual report and proxy.

checklist.step: Fix which exchange listing standard the written policy must satisfy
actions: Read the securities registered under Section 12(b) from the current Form 10-K cover page and note the exchange on which each class of common equity is listed.

Open NYSE Listed Company Manual Section 303A.14 or Nasdaq Rule 5608 on the exchange's rulebook site and copy the required policy terms table (covered executives, three-year lookback, recovery obligation, permitted impracticability grounds) into the review memo.
Ask Investor Relations to confirm no class was delisted or moved during the year, which would change the governing standard.
Save the review memo to the board portal Compensation Committee folder as clawback-standard-review-<fiscal year>.
checklist.done: the governing exchange standard is identified from the 10-K cover page and its required-terms table is captured in the dated review memo.

checklist.step: Re-read Rule 10D-1 and Item 402(w) against the current published text
actions: Open 17 CFR 240.10D-1 and 17 CFR 229.402(w) on eCFR and record the amendment date shown at the top of each section.

Redline the current policy text against the rule's mandatory elements: accounting-restatement definition covering both Big-R and little-r, three-completed-fiscal-year lookback, no-fault application, and the exhaustive impracticability grounds.
Note in the memo any SEC Compliance and Disclosure Interpretation issued since the last review that changes the reading.
File the dated redline in iManage under Corporate Governance ▸ Clawback and send it to the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: a dated redline of the policy against the current 10D-1 and Item 402(w) text is filed, with every mandatory element mapped to a policy clause.

checklist.step: Rebuild the covered executive officer population for the lookback period
actions: Extract from the HRIS every holder of a Section 16 officer title with effective-from and effective-to dates covering the three completed fiscal years.
Reconcile the extract to the Section 16 officer list the Corporate Secretary maintains for Forms 3/4/5 and to the named executive officer table in the last proxy.
Add former officers who served any part of the lookback period — the policy reaches them and departures are the usual gap.
Publish the reconciled roster with a sign-off line from the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: a reconciled covered-officer roster spans the full three-year lookback and includes leavers, signed by the Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: Inventory the incentive awards that are based on a financial reporting measure
actions: List every annual bonus, performance share unit and cash LTI award paid or vested to a covered officer in the lookback period, with grant date, performance period, metric and payout amount.
Tag each metric as a financial reporting measure (revenue, combined ratio, adjusted EPS, statutory surplus growth, total shareholder return) or not, and record the reason for each non-tag.
Pull the payout amounts from the payroll register and the equity administrator's vest report so the amounts tie to cash actually delivered.
Hand the tagged inventory to the Controller as the base for any future erroneously-awarded-amount computation.
checklist.done: every lookback-period incentive payout is listed, tagged as financial-reporting-measure based or not, and tied to payroll or vest records.

checklist.step: Refresh the written policy text and its operating procedure
actions: Update the policy to close every gap the Regulatory Counsel redline identified, keeping the mandatory no-fault language intact.

Update the operating procedure appendix with the trigger intake path from the close process, the computation method for each award type, and the recovery methods available (payroll offset, forfeiture of unvested awards, direct repayment on a stated schedule).
Circulate to the Chief Financial Officer and Chief HR Officer for comment with a five-business-day turnaround and log the comments received.
Version the document as v<n>-<fiscal year> in iManage and lock the prior version read-only.
checklist.done: a versioned policy and operating procedure exist in iManage with every redline gap closed and CFO and HR comments logged.

checklist.step: Take the policy through the Compensation Committee and the Board
actions: Load the policy, the redline and the review memo into the Compensation Committee book in the board portal at least seven days before the Q1 meeting.
Present the changes and the exchange standard mapping, and record the committee's recommendation in the draft minutes.
Obtain the Board resolution adopting the policy and capture the resolution number and adoption date.
Publish the adopted version to the governance page of the intranet and to the investor relations governance documents page.
checklist.done: the Board resolution adopting the current policy version is recorded with its date and the adopted text is published internally and externally.

checklist.step: Collect a signed acknowledgement from every covered officer
actions: Send the adopted policy plus the acknowledgement form through DocuSign to every officer on the reconciled roster, with a 14-day completion deadline.
Add the acknowledgement to the new-hire and promotion packet for Section 16 officers so future appointees sign before their first award.
Chase non-signers at day 7 and day 12 and escalate any officer still outstanding at day 14 to the General Counsel.
File the executed envelopes against each officer's record and update the roster's acknowledgement column.
checklist.done: every covered officer has an executed acknowledgement on file, or an outstanding signer is escalated to the General Counsel.

checklist.step: Wire the restatement trigger into the financial close and disclosure process
actions: Add a standing close checklist item: 'Restatement or non-reliance conclusion reached this period? Y/N' with the Controller as signer each quarter.
Define the escalation path: a Y answer notifies the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel within 2 business days and opens the clawback assessment file.
Include both a Big-R restatement (Form 8-K Item 4.02 non-reliance) and a little-r revision of prior-period figures in the trigger definition.
Confirm with the external auditor's engagement partner that any proposed audit adjustment reaching restatement is reported to the Audit Committee the same week.
checklist.done: the close checklist carries a signed restatement/non-reliance question each quarter with a defined 2-business-day escalation to the Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: Compute the erroneously awarded compensation when a trigger fires
actions: Take the restated financial reporting measure values from the Controller and recompute each affected award's payout as it would have been on the corrected figures.
Set erroneously awarded compensation for each award to the pre-tax excess of the amount received over the recomputed amount, per officer per award.

For share-price or TSR-based awards, document the reasonable estimate of the restatement's effect on the price or TSR outcome and keep the working file, since that estimate must be furnished to the exchange.
Have the Controller review and initial the computation before it goes to the Compensation Committee.
checklist.done: a per-officer, per-award erroneously-awarded-amount computation exists, on a pre-tax basis, reviewed and initialled by the Controller.

checklist.step: Select the recovery method and set the collection schedule
actions: Present the recovery options to the Compensation Committee: forfeiture of unvested awards, offset against future incentive payouts, payroll deduction where state wage law allows, or a direct repayment note.
Confirm with Employment Counsel that the chosen method is lawful in the officer's work state before it is executed.
Record the approved method, the instalment amounts and the final collection date in the recovery file and notify the officer in writing.
Open a receivable in the general ledger for any amount not recovered by immediate forfeiture.
checklist.done: a committee-approved, counsel-cleared recovery method with an instalment schedule and a general-ledger receivable exists for each affected officer.

checklist.step: Document any impracticability claim against the rule's exhaustive grounds
actions: Limit the claim to the grounds the rule allows: direct expense of enforcement paid to a third party would exceed the amount recovered, or recovery would violate home-country law adopted before 28 November 2022.
Obtain and attach the third-party invoice or fee estimate, or the home-country legal opinion, that supports the ground claimed.
Confirm a reasonable attempt to recover was actually made and documented before the claim is raised.
Have the Compensation Committee approve the determination, then furnish the required explanation to the exchange and disclose it under Item 402(w).
checklist.done: each impracticability determination cites an allowed ground, carries its supporting invoice or legal opinion, and has committee approval plus an exchange notification.

checklist.step: Execute collection and track the balance to zero
actions: Set up the approved deduction or repayment schedule against the officer's payroll record with the start date and instalment amount from the recovery file.
Reconcile each instalment posted to the general-ledger receivable monthly with the Senior Accountant and report the remaining balance.
Flag any missed instalment to the Compensation & Benefits Manager within five business days of the pay date.
Close the recovery file only when the receivable is zero and the Controller confirms the write-off, if any, was committee-approved.
checklist.done: the recovery receivable is reconciled monthly and the file is closed only at a zero balance or a committee-approved write-off.

checklist.step: File Exhibit 97 and complete the 10-K cover-page clawback boxes
actions: Attach the current board-adopted policy to the Form 10-K exhibit index as Exhibit 97 and confirm the exhibit tag renders in the EDGAR submission preview.
Tick the two cover-page check-boxes: whether the filing reflects correction of an error to previously issued financial statements, and whether that correction required a recovery analysis.
Draft the Item 402(w) narrative for the proxy where a restatement occurred, covering the amount, the date of the analysis and any outstanding balance by officer.
Have the General Counsel clear the exhibit and the narrative before the filing is transmitted through EDGAR.
checklist.done: the 10-K carries Exhibit 97, both cover-page boxes are answered consistently with the restatement log, and the Item 402(w) narrative is GC-cleared.

checklist.step: Refresh the written information-security program documents in the same annual cycle
actions: Open the information-security program document set in the GRC platform and review each policy whose review date falls within the fiscal year.
Record the reviewer, review date and any change to control ownership on each document record.
Map the program documents to the Reg S-K Item 106 disclosure statements so the 10-K description is supported by an approved policy behind every claim.
Report the completed review to the Audit Committee with the count of documents reviewed, changed and overdue.
checklist.done: every in-scope security program document carries a dated annual review, and each Item 106 disclosure statement maps to an approved document.

checklist.step: File the evidence set and apply the retention label
actions: Move the board resolution, adopted policy version, acknowledgement roster and executed envelopes, recovery computations and impracticability memos into the repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set the legal-hold flag on any file connected to an open restatement or SEC inquiry.
Confirm the index makes the record searchable by fiscal year, officer name and award type.
Send the Corporate Secretary the repository link that will be quoted in any regulator response.
checklist.done: the full evidence set is filed under a 7-year retention label and retrievable by fiscal year, officer and award type.

testing.step: Build the population of covered officers, awards and restatement events
actions: Extract independently from the HRIS every Section 16 officer with service dates inside the three completed fiscal years, without using the roster Compensation prepared.
Extract every incentive payout and equity vest to those officers from payroll and the equity administrator's vest report.
Pull the restatement log and every Form 8-K Item 4.02 filed in the period from the financial reporting repository.
Record the extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently extracted population of officers, awards and restatement events exists with documented filters and row counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the Section 16 records and the proxy
actions: Match the officer extract to the Forms 3, 4 and 5 filed on EDGAR for the period and to the named executive officer table in each proxy.
Investigate every officer appearing in one source and not the others, particularly mid-year appointments and departures.
Tie total incentive payouts in the extract to the Summary Compensation Table totals and explain differences by component.
Sign the reconciliation as complete before any sample is drawn.
testing.done: the population ties to Section 16 filings and the Summary Compensation Table with every difference explained and signed off.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of officers affected by any restatement event in the period and 100% of impracticability determinations.
Take 15 additional awards at random, using a recorded seed, from the unaffected population to test acknowledgement and metric tagging.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection method so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Note any population stratum deliberately excluded and why.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all restatement-affected officers and all impracticability claims is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the erroneously awarded amount computation
actions: Take the restated measure values from the filed amended financial statements, not from the Compensation working file.
Recompute each sampled award's payout on the corrected figures and derive the pre-tax excess independently.
Compare to the recorded amount; any difference over $1,000 or any use of a post-tax basis is an exception.
For share-price or TSR awards, challenge the reasonableness of the estimate method and confirm the working file supporting it was furnished to the exchange.
testing.done: each sampled recovery amount is independently recomputed on a pre-tax basis and agreed, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the policy text against the rule and the listing standard
actions: Read the board-adopted policy against 17 CFR 240.10D-1 and the applicable NYSE 303A.14 or Nasdaq 5608 text as they read on the adoption date.
Confirm the policy is no-fault, covers little-r revisions as well as Big-R restatements, and runs a three-completed-fiscal-year lookback.
Confirm the impracticability grounds in the policy are not broader than the rule allows — an added ground is a fail, not a drafting nuance.
Record the clause-by-clause mapping in the workpaper.
testing.done: every mandatory rule element maps to a policy clause and no impracticability ground exceeds what the rule permits.

testing.step: Trace the Exhibit 97 filing and the cover-page answers
actions: Open the filed Form 10-K on EDGAR and confirm Exhibit 97 is present in the exhibit index and opens to the board-adopted version, not a draft.
Compare the two cover-page check-box answers to the restatement log for the year; an unchecked box against a logged restatement is a reportable failure.
Where a recovery occurred, read the Item 402(w) narrative in the proxy and confirm the amounts and dates match the recovery file.
Capture the EDGAR filing index and the exhibit's first page into the workpaper.
testing.done: the filed Exhibit 97 matches the adopted policy version and the cover-page answers agree with the restatement log.

testing.step: Test acknowledgements and roster completeness
actions: For each sampled officer, open the DocuSign envelope and confirm the signature date is on or after the adoption date of the version they signed.
Confirm officers appointed during the year signed before their first incentive award was granted.
List any officer on the reconciled roster with no envelope as an exception with the days outstanding.
Check that departed officers' acknowledgements were retained rather than purged with the HR record.
testing.done: every sampled officer has an envelope signed against the correct policy version, and gaps are listed with days outstanding.

testing.step: Recompute the lookback window and the recovery schedule dates
actions: Recompute the lookback as the three completed fiscal years preceding the date the board concluded a restatement was required, and compare it to the window Compensation used.
Check that a transition period of nine months or more was treated as a completed fiscal year where applicable.
Compare each recovery instalment date and amount in the payroll record to the approved schedule and quantify any slippage in days.
Confirm the general-ledger receivable balance agrees with the recovery file at the test date.
testing.done: the lookback window and every instalment date reconcile to the approved schedule and the receivable balance agrees.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the officer, the award, the amount at risk and the disclosure consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: roster gap, metric mis-tagged, trigger not escalated from close, computation error, or acknowledgement not chased.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any unrecovered amount to the General Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and state the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Confirm the reviewer signing the workpaper prepared none of the sampled computations or memos.
Report the conclusion and any unrecovered balance to the Compensation Committee and the Audit Committee at their next meetings.
File the signed workpaper with its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rate, and both committees have a recorded reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: CISO owns the enterprise cybersecurity risk assessment and the remediation backlog behind it; the Corporate Secretary owns the Reg S-K Item 106 wording that describes it in the Form 10-K.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-K Item 106, 17 CFR 229.106 read on eCFR alongside the SEC's Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance and Incident Disclosure adopting release, re-verified before each 10-K drafting cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Annual enterprise cybersecurity risk assessment across underwriting, policy administration, claims, billing and finance systems; the vulnerability and penetration-test remediation cycle feeding it; and the board and management oversight routines described in the Item 106(c) disclosure.

In-scope systems.value: Risk register, control assessments and remediation plans in the GRC platform; scan findings from Qualys/Tenable; detection coverage evidence from the SIEM.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Procedure — asset and crown-jewel scoping, threat scenario library, likelihood and impact scoring, control effectiveness rating, residual-risk acceptance route, and the mapping from assessment output to the Item 106(b) narrative.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and ratified by the Audit Committee at the meeting where the annual assessment is presented; refreshed on any change to the assessment framework.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Assessment completed and presented to the Audit Committee no later than 60 days before the 10-K filing date; the Item 106 disclosure is filed with the Form 10-K each year within the filer-status deadline after fiscal year end.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Assessment kick-off task at fiscal year end minus 150 days, draft-to-disclosure handover at minus 75 days, and remediation milestone alerts at 30, 15 and 5 days before each finding's committed date.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Assessment report, scoring workbook, threat scenario library version, remediation tickets, board slides and the Item 106 disclosure support file retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Overdue high or critical findings, assets never assessed, and any Item 106 statement not supported by an assessment artifact are logged as exceptions with owner, disposition and a re-presentation date to the Audit Committee.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs every residual-risk acceptance and every closed critical finding before the assessment is presented to the Audit Committee.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All in-scope information assets and business applications on the assessment scope list for the fiscal year, every high or critical finding raised in the year, and every factual statement made in the filed Item 106 disclosure.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A fail is any crown-jewel asset absent from the assessment scope, any critical finding past its committed date without a CRO-signed acceptance, or any Item 106 sentence with no supporting artifact; more than 5% of findings overdue escalates to the Audit Committee.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs annually in the quarter before the 10-K, with a quarterly interim check on remediation ageing because findings move between annual cycles.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Information Security and must not have scored any sampled risk or owned any sampled finding.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Item 106 assurance workpaper — scope reconciliation, sampled scoring re-performance, finding ageing analysis and the disclosure-to-artifact trace — in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment report, Audit Committee minutes showing the oversight described in Item 106(c), remediation ageing report and the disclosure support matrix, producible to an SEC comment letter within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary drafts the response to any SEC Division of Corporation Finance comment on the Item 106 disclosure; the CISO supplies the technical support and the General Counsel clears the response before it is filed as CORRESP on EDGAR.

checklist.step: Set the assessment scope from the asset and application inventory
actions: Export from the CMDB every application and infrastructure service with a business-criticality rating, owner and hosting model.
Ask each business owner — Underwriting, Claims, Billing, Actuarial, Finance — to confirm which of their systems hold policyholder or claimant personal data and which support financial reporting.
Mark crown-jewel assets: the policy administration platform, claims platform, billing platform, general ledger and the data warehouse holding customer records.
Publish the scope list with a version number and circulate it to the CISO for approval before fieldwork starts.
checklist.done: a versioned, CISO-approved scope list names every crown-jewel asset with its business owner and data classification.

checklist.step: Refresh the threat scenario library for the insurance operating model
actions: Review the prior-year scenario library and add scenarios seen in the year's telemetry: broker-portal credential stuffing, claims-payment business email compromise, ransomware on the policy administration estate, and third-party administrator data exposure.
Pull supporting frequency data from the SIEM for each scenario — blocked authentication anomalies, phishing click rates, detection counts by MITRE ATT&CK technique.
Cross-check the library against the sector advisories the FS-ISAC circulated during the year and record which were adopted.
Version the library and attach it to the assessment file as the basis for likelihood scoring.
checklist.done: a versioned threat scenario library backed by the year's SIEM telemetry and sector advisories is attached to the assessment file.

checklist.step: Score likelihood and impact for every in-scope asset and scenario
actions: Open the risk register in Archer and create one assessment record per asset-scenario pair on the approved scope list.
Score likelihood on the published 1-5 scale using the scenario frequency data, and impact on financial, policyholder-harm, regulatory and reputational axes.
Record the reasoning sentence and the evidence link on every score — an unexplained score cannot support a disclosure statement.
Route scores above the inherent-risk threshold to the asset owner for challenge and record their response.
checklist.done: every asset-scenario pair carries a scored, evidenced and owner-challenged risk record in Archer.

checklist.step: Rate the effectiveness of the controls that reduce each risk
actions: Map each risk to the controls that mitigate it — MFA, privileged access management, encryption at rest and in transit, endpoint detection, network segmentation, backup immutability.
Rate each control design and operating effectiveness using the most recent test result, and record the test date so stale evidence is visible.
Where the latest test is older than 12 months, mark the control 'not evidenced' rather than assuming it works.
Compute residual risk from inherent score and control rating using the published method and publish the residual heat map.
checklist.done: every risk has mapped controls with dated effectiveness ratings and a computed residual score, with stale evidence marked not evidenced.

checklist.step: Feed vulnerability and penetration-test results into the assessment
actions: Export the current authenticated-scan results for every in-scope asset and summarise open critical and high findings by asset and age.
Add the findings from the year's external penetration test and any red-team exercise, with the tester's risk rating.
Reconcile the scanned asset list to the assessment scope list and raise coverage gaps — an unscanned crown-jewel asset is itself a finding.
Attach the summary to the corresponding risk records so the residual score reflects real exposure.
checklist.done: scan and penetration-test findings are attached to the risk records and every scope-list asset is confirmed as scanned or raised as a coverage gap.

checklist.step: Build the remediation plan with named owners and committed dates
actions: Raise one remediation ticket per finding with the asset, the risk it drives, the fix and the business owner accepting the date.
Apply the standard service levels — critical within 30 days, high within 90 days — and record any owner-negotiated extension with its reason.
Link each ticket back to its Archer risk record so closing the ticket updates the residual score.
Publish a weekly ageing report to the CISO showing overdue criticals by owner.
checklist.done: every finding has a linked ticket with a named owner and a committed date within the service level or a recorded extension.

checklist.step: Route residual risks above appetite for formal acceptance
actions: List every residual risk above the board-set appetite threshold with its score, driver and the compensating controls in place.
Prepare an acceptance record per risk stating the acceptance period, the review date and the conditions that would revoke it.
Obtain the Chief Risk Officer signature on each acceptance and the business owner's countersignature.
Report the accepted-risk inventory to the Risk Committee and record the meeting date on each record.
checklist.done: every above-appetite residual risk has a dated, CRO-signed acceptance with an expiry and a committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Test that the assessment covers third-party and outsourced processing
actions: List the third parties that process policyholder or claimant data — third-party administrators, cloud hosting, print and mail vendors, medical bill review, salvage and subrogation vendors.
For each, record the most recent SOC 2 Type II report date, the exceptions noted and whether they were remediated.
Score third-party scenarios in the same register rather than in a separate file, since Item 106(b) asks about processes for risks from third-party providers.
Flag any critical vendor with no current assurance report as an assessment finding.
checklist.done: third-party processing risks are scored in the same register and every critical vendor has a current assurance report or a raised finding.

checklist.step: Write the assessment report and the management summary
actions: Summarise the scope, method, top residual risks, movement since the prior year and the remediation position with counts by severity and ageing.

State plainly whether any risk from cybersecurity threats has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the business strategy, results of operations or financial condition — this is the Item 106(b)(2) conclusion.
Have the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel review the wording of that conclusion before it is circulated.
Circulate the report to the Audit Committee pack at least seven days before the meeting.
checklist.done: a report exists with a reviewed materiality conclusion in the Item 106(b)(2) form, circulated ahead of the Audit Committee meeting.

checklist.step: Present to the Audit Committee and record the oversight evidence
actions: Load the report and slides into the board portal and confirm the agenda item names cybersecurity risk oversight explicitly.
Ensure the minutes record which committee holds oversight, how often it is briefed, and the process by which management informs it — the three facts Item 106(c) requires.
Capture the names and relevant expertise of the management personnel who presented, since Item 106(c)(2) asks for it.
File the approved minutes extract in the disclosure support folder.
checklist.done: the minutes evidence the committee, the briefing cadence, the escalation process and the presenters' expertise, and an extract is in the disclosure support folder.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 106 disclosure and build the support matrix
actions: Draft Item 106(b) covering the processes for assessing, identifying and managing material risks, whether they are integrated into the overall risk management system, whether assessors, consultants or auditors are engaged, and the third-party oversight process.
Draft Item 106(c) covering board oversight, the responsible committee and management's role and expertise.
Build a support matrix that maps every sentence of the draft to a named artifact — assessment report page, minutes extract, procedure version or ticket report.
Send any sentence with no artifact back to the CISO for evidence or deletion before the disclosure is cleared.
checklist.done: the Item 106 draft exists with a sentence-by-sentence support matrix and no unsupported statement remains.

checklist.step: Clear the disclosure through the Disclosure Committee and legal review
actions: Circulate the Item 106 draft and support matrix to the Disclosure Committee with the CFO, Controller, CISO and Investor Relations Director.
Challenge any statement that overstates maturity relative to the open critical findings — the ageing report is the check.
Confirm the description does not disclose specifics that would impede incident response or remediation, as the adopting release permits withholding.
Record the committee's clearance and the date in the minutes and file them in iManage.
checklist.done: the Disclosure Committee has cleared the Item 106 text against the support matrix and the ageing report, with the clearance minuted.

checklist.step: File the disclosure with the Form 10-K and archive the support
actions: Place the cleared Item 106 text into Part I of the Form 10-K and confirm the section renders and tags correctly in the EDGAR submission preview.
Confirm the filing goes out within the filer-status deadline after fiscal year end and record the EDGAR accession number.
Archive the as-filed text with its support matrix in the disclosure support folder.
Notify the CISO of the accession number so the assessment file references the filing it supported.
checklist.done: the Item 106 disclosure is filed within the deadline and the as-filed text plus support matrix are archived against the accession number.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure through the year
actions: Run the ageing report monthly and escalate any critical finding past 30 days to the asset owner's executive.
Require evidence of fix — a rescan result, a configuration export or a control retest — before a ticket is closed, not an owner's assertion.
Re-score the linked Archer risk when a ticket closes so the residual heat map stays current between annual cycles.
Report closure rates and overdue counts to the Audit Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: findings close only on retest evidence, linked risks are re-scored, and quarterly ageing is reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: File the assessment evidence set under retention
actions: Move the scope list, scoring workbook, threat library version, scan exports, acceptance records, minutes extract and support matrix into the repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set legal hold on anything connected to an open incident or SEC inquiry.
Confirm the record is searchable by fiscal year, asset name and finding severity.
Send the repository link to the Corporate Secretary for use in regulator responses.
checklist.done: the assessment evidence set is filed under a 7-year label and searchable by fiscal year, asset and severity.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope assets, findings and disclosure statements
actions: Extract the full application and infrastructure inventory from the CMDB at the assessment date, independently of the scope list Security produced.
Extract every high and critical finding raised in the fiscal year from the ticketing system with raise date, committed date and closure date.
Split the filed Item 106 disclosure into individual factual statements and number them.
Record extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent populations of assets, findings and numbered disclosure statements exist with documented extract parameters.

testing.step: Reconcile the assessment scope to the asset inventory
actions: Match the approved scope list to the CMDB extract and list every asset in the inventory but not in scope.
For each omission, ask the CISO for the documented rationale and judge it against the crown-jewel criteria.
Treat any system holding policyholder or claimant personal data, or supporting financial reporting, that was excluded without written rationale as an automatic exception.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every inventory asset is either in scope or has a written, judged exclusion rationale, and the reconciliation is signed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of crown-jewel assets and 100% of critical findings raised in the year.
Take 20 high findings and 15 asset-scenario risk records at random using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of the numbered Item 106 disclosure statements for the support trace.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all crown-jewel assets, all criticals and all disclosure statements is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk scoring on the sampled records
actions: Open each sampled risk record in Archer and read the evidence links without first reading the recorded score.
Apply the published likelihood and impact scale independently and reach your own residual rating.
Compare to the recorded rating; a difference of more than one band, or a score with no reasoning sentence, is an exception.
Capture the record screen and your scoring note into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled risk has an independent re-scored rating and any band difference or missing rationale is logged.

testing.step: Verify control effectiveness ratings against real test evidence
actions: For each sampled risk, open the control test evidence behind the effectiveness rating and check its date is within 12 months of the assessment.
Re-run or read the current authenticated scan result for the asset and compare the exposure to the rating claimed.
Where a control is rated effective but the asset carries open criticals, log the contradiction as an exception.
Confirm controls with no dated evidence were marked 'not evidenced' rather than assumed effective.
testing.done: every sampled control rating is supported by evidence dated within 12 months and contradicted ratings are logged.

testing.step: Trace every Item 106 statement to a named artifact
actions: Take each numbered disclosure statement and open the artifact the support matrix cites for it.
Confirm the artifact predates the filing date and actually says what the statement claims — a procedure that exists but was never executed does not support a claim of process.
Check the Item 106(c) statements against the Audit Committee minutes for committee identity, briefing cadence and escalation process.
Log any statement with no artifact, a post-dated artifact or an artifact that does not carry the claim.
testing.done: every filed Item 106 statement traces to a pre-dated artifact that supports it, or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Test third-party coverage inside the assessment
actions: Take the critical vendor list from Procurement and check each appears as a scored scenario in the same risk register.
For five vendors, open the SOC 2 Type II report and confirm the period covers the fiscal year and the exceptions were dispositioned.
Confirm any vendor with no current report was raised as a finding rather than left unscored.
Record the coverage percentage of critical vendors assessed.
testing.done: critical vendors are scored in the register with current assurance reports or raised findings, and coverage is quantified.

testing.step: Recompute remediation ageing against the service levels
actions: Recompute days open for every sampled finding as closure date minus raise date, or test date minus raise date if still open.
Compare to the 30-day critical and 90-day high service levels and count breaches by owner.
For closed tickets, open the closure evidence and confirm it is a rescan or retest result rather than an owner assertion.
Check that every extension beyond the service level carries a recorded reason and an approver.
testing.done: ageing is independently recomputed, breaches are counted by owner, and every closure carries retest evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the asset or statement, the gap and the disclosure consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: scope omission, stale control evidence, unsupported disclosure sentence, vendor not assessed, or service-level breach.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route unsupported disclosure statements to the General Counsel for an amendment assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the overdue-finding rate against the 5% threshold and state the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Confirm the signer scored no sampled risk and owned no sampled finding.
Report the conclusion, the unsupported-statement count and the overdue criticals to the Audit Committee at its next meeting.
File the signed workpaper and its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and overdue rate, and the Audit Committee has a recorded reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: IT Security Manager owns continuous operation of the MFA, encryption and access-review controls; the Ethics Officer owns the Item 406 code of ethics whose availability and waiver reporting is this item's pass condition, with the Corporate Secretary filing the Form 8-K.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-K Item 406, 17 CFR 229.406 (code of ethics, availability and waiver disclosure), Regulation FD, 17 CFR 243.100, and Rule 14a-21 read on eCFR at each annual refresh; Form 8-K Item 5.05 instructions checked for the waiver reporting route.

In-scope processes.value: Continuous identity and data-protection operations — MFA enrolment and enforcement, encryption key management, privileged access management and quarterly user access reviews across the policy administration, claims, billing and general ledger systems — and the code of ethics lifecycle covering the CEO, CFO, principal accounting officer and controller.

In-scope systems.value: MFA policy and enforcement in the IAM platform, certification campaigns in SailPoint IGA, privileged credentials in CyberArk, and the code of ethics plus attestations in the learning management system.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Access Control and Data Protection Standard (MFA coverage rules, encryption standards for data at rest and in transit, quarterly certification cadence, revocation service levels) plus the Code of Ethics Administration Procedure covering waiver requests, approval authority and the four-business-day 8-K route.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Access standard approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and reviewed annually; the code of ethics adopted by the Board and re-approved annually, with any amendment reported alongside waivers.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Access certification campaigns close within 30 days of each quarter end so evidence supports the Rule 13a-13 Form 10-Q filed within 45 days of quarter end; the Item 406 disclosure and website availability statement go with the Form 10-K filed within 90 days after fiscal year end; any waiver or amendment is reported on Form 8-K Item 5.05 within four business days.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Certification campaign opens on day 1 after quarter end with reviewer reminders at day 10, 20 and 27; a waiver-request alert routes to the Corporate Secretary the same day it is raised so the four-business-day 8-K clock is visible from hour one.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certification campaign exports with reviewer decisions, MFA coverage reports, encryption configuration attestations, code of ethics versions, officer attestation records and filed waiver 8-Ks retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Accounts without MFA, unencrypted stores, revocations missed beyond service level, uncertified entitlements and any waiver granted without an 8-K are logged as exceptions with owner, disposition and quarter of closure.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CISO signs off closure of every MFA or encryption gap on a covered system; the General Counsel signs off every code of ethics waiver and its disclosure treatment.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All active user and service accounts on in-scope financial and policyholder systems at quarter end, all privileged accounts, all data stores classified confidential or above, and every code of ethics waiver or amendment granted in the year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A fail is any interactive account on an in-scope system without MFA, any confidential data store without encryption at rest, any leaver with access beyond 24 hours of termination, or any waiver granted to a covered officer without a Form 8-K Item 5.05 within four business days; certification completion below 100% by day 30 is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Controls are continuous, so the test runs quarterly against the quarter-end population and feeds the 10-Q disclosure-controls conclusion; the code of ethics elements are tested annually before the 10-K and event-driven on every waiver.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly access-controls workpaper and the annual code of ethics workpaper — population extracts, sample, re-performance notes, exception log — in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the SOX control test binder.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Certification campaign exports, MFA and encryption coverage reports, the published code of ethics with its website URL, the officer attestation roster and any filed Item 5.05 8-K, producible to an SEC comment letter or an auditor's request within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary answers SEC comments on the Item 406 disclosure through EDGAR correspondence; the CISO supplies control evidence to the external auditor and the Audit Committee; the General Counsel clears any statement about a granted waiver before release.

checklist.step: Define the in-scope account and data-store population
actions: List from the CMDB every application flagged as financially significant or holding policyholder data — policy administration, claims, billing, general ledger, data warehouse, broker portal.
For each, record the authentication source, whether it federates to the IAM platform, and its data classification.
Ask each application owner to confirm the service and integration accounts that cannot take interactive MFA, with a compensating control named for each.
Publish the scope register and have the IT Security Manager approve it for the year.
checklist.done: an approved scope register names every in-scope system with its authentication source, data classification and exempted service accounts.

checklist.step: Enforce MFA policy across the in-scope estate
actions: In the IAM platform open the sign-on policy for each in-scope application and set MFA required for all interactive access, with phishing-resistant factors mandated for administrators.
Run the MFA coverage report and list every enabled human account without an enrolled factor.
Give each application owner a 10-business-day window to enrol or justify, then disable unenrolled accounts.
Export the post-enforcement coverage report and file it as the quarter's MFA evidence.
checklist.done: the coverage report shows every interactive account on in-scope systems with an enrolled factor, or the account disabled.

checklist.step: Verify encryption of data at rest and in transit on covered stores
actions: Export the encryption configuration for each confidential data store — database transparent data encryption state, storage-account encryption, key source and rotation date.
Confirm TLS 1.2 or above is enforced on every external endpoint by reading the load balancer and API gateway listener configuration.
List any store with encryption off, a key past its rotation interval, or a legacy cipher enabled, and raise a ticket per store.
Have the application owner attest to the configuration in writing and file the attestation with the export.
checklist.done: every confidential store has a dated encryption configuration export, a current key rotation, and an owner attestation on file.

checklist.step: Bring privileged accounts under managed vaulting and session control
actions: Reconcile the privileged account inventory in CyberArk to the local administrator and database sysadmin lists exported from each in-scope system.
Onboard any unvaulted privileged credential, set automatic rotation, and enable session recording for administrative access to financial systems.
Convert standing administrator rights to just-in-time elevation with an approval step wherever the platform supports it.
Publish the residual standing-privilege list to the IT Security Manager each month.
checklist.done: every privileged credential on an in-scope system is vaulted with rotation and session recording, and residual standing privilege is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly user access certification campaign
actions: Open a certification campaign in SailPoint on day 1 after quarter end covering all in-scope applications, with the line manager as first reviewer and the application owner as second.
Present each entitlement with its business role, last-used date and toxic-combination flags so reviewers decide on facts rather than names.
Send reminders at day 10, 20 and 27 and escalate incomplete reviewers to their director at day 25.
Close the campaign by day 30 and export the decision file as the quarter's certification evidence.
checklist.done: the campaign closes by day 30 of the quarter with a 100% decision rate and an exported decision file.

checklist.step: Revoke every access the certification rejected and prove it
actions: Generate the revocation work items from the campaign decisions and route them to the fulfilling team automatically where a connector exists.
Track manual revocations to a 5-business-day service level and chase daily past day 3.
Re-query the target system after each revocation and attach the query result to the work item as proof of removal.
List any revocation still open at day 10 as an exception with the entitlement and the owner.
checklist.done: every rejected entitlement is removed with a post-removal system query attached, or listed as an exception past day 10.

checklist.step: Tie joiner-mover-leaver events to access changes within service level
actions: Take the daily termination and transfer feed from the HRIS into the IAM platform and confirm the connector ran without error each day.
Disable leaver accounts within 24 hours of the termination effective date and revoke transferred users' prior-role entitlements within 5 business days.
Reconcile the month's terminations from the HRIS to disabled accounts and investigate every unmatched row.
Report the reconciliation result to the IT Security Manager monthly.
checklist.done: every termination in the HRIS reconciles to a disabled account within 24 hours and transfers are re-entitled within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Monitor control operation continuously and alert on drift
actions: Build detections for MFA policy bypass, new local administrator creation, encryption disabled on a monitored store and privileged access outside CyberArk.
Route each detection to the ITSM queue with the owning application and a 24-hour triage service level.
Publish a weekly control-drift dashboard showing detections by control and by system.
Feed confirmed drift into the quarterly exception log rather than closing it silently.
checklist.done: drift detections exist for each key control, are triaged within 24 hours, and confirmed drift lands in the quarterly exception log.

checklist.step: Adopt and publish the code of ethics for the senior financial officers
actions: Confirm the code applies expressly to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller, and persons performing similar functions, as Item 406(b) requires.
Publish the current version on the investor relations governance page and record the exact URL that will be named in the 10-K.
Where the company chooses to satisfy availability by undertaking to provide a copy without charge, record that undertaking wording instead.
Confirm the published version matches the board-approved version byte for byte before the 10-K is drafted.
checklist.done: the code covering the named officer positions is published at a recorded URL and matches the board-approved version.

checklist.step: Collect annual officer and employee attestations to the code
actions: Assign the code of ethics module and attestation in the learning management system to all officers and employees with a 30-day completion window.
Track completion by department weekly and escalate incomplete senior financial officers to the General Counsel at day 21.
Export the completion roster with names, titles and attestation dates as the annual evidence.
Record any disclosed conflict from the attestation questionnaire and route it to the Ethics Officer for disposition.
checklist.done: the attestation roster shows every covered officer completed within 30 days, with disclosed conflicts routed for disposition.

checklist.step: Run the waiver request path and start the four-business-day clock
actions: Open a case for any request for a waiver or implicit waiver from a code provision by a covered officer or a director, capturing the provision, the facts and the requester.
Notify the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel the same day the request is raised so the disclosure clock is visible before any decision is made.
Route the decision to the Audit Committee or the Board as the code requires and record the decision date — that date starts the four-business-day Form 8-K Item 5.05 clock.
Record a denied request as closed with reasons; a denial carries no disclosure obligation but the case must still be retained.
checklist.done: every waiver request is a case with the provision, the deciding body, the decision date and a same-day notification to the Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: File the Form 8-K Item 5.05 for any waiver or amendment
actions: Draft the Item 5.05 disclosure naming the person, the date, the nature of the waiver and the provision waived, or describing the amendment.
Confirm with the General Counsel whether the alternative website-disclosure method previously stated in the 10-K is being used, and if so post within the same four-business-day window.
Transmit the 8-K through EDGAR within four business days of the decision date and record the accession number against the case.
Close the case only when the accession number or the website posting URL is attached.
checklist.done: each waiver or amendment has a Form 8-K Item 5.05 or the elected website posting within four business days, with the reference attached to the case.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 406 disclosure and the disclosure-controls support
actions: State in the Form 10-K whether a code of ethics has been adopted for the named officer positions and, if not, why not.
State the availability method — the website URL, the intention to file it as an exhibit, or the undertaking to provide a copy without charge — exactly as elected.
Attach the quarterly certification exports and MFA and encryption coverage reports to the disclosure-controls evidence file supporting the Rule 13a-15 conclusion.
Have the Disclosure Committee clear both the Item 406 wording and the controls conclusion before filing.
checklist.done: the Item 406 disclosure states adoption, coverage and availability as elected, and the controls evidence file supports the disclosure-controls conclusion.

checklist.step: Report control health to the Audit Committee each quarter
actions: Prepare a pack showing MFA coverage percentage, encryption exceptions, certification completion rate, revocation service-level performance and open exception counts.
Show the movement since the prior quarter and name owners of any control operating below target.
Load the pack into the board portal at least seven days before the meeting and record the minutes reference.
Feed any control the committee challenges into the next quarter's remediation plan with a named owner.
checklist.done: a quarterly control-health pack with coverage, completion and exception metrics is minuted at the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: File the quarterly and annual evidence under retention
actions: Move the certification exports, revocation proofs, MFA and encryption reports, attestation roster, waiver cases and filed 8-Ks into the repository under the quarter or fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and legal hold on anything connected to an open inquiry or restatement.
Confirm the record is searchable by quarter, application name and officer name.
Give the external auditor read access to the quarter's folder for the interim controls walkthrough.
checklist.done: each quarter's control evidence and the annual code evidence are filed under a 7-year label and available to the external auditor.

testing.step: Build the quarter-end account, data-store and waiver population
actions: Extract all active accounts on in-scope systems as at quarter end directly from the target systems, not from the IAM aggregation, so unfederated accounts appear.
Extract the confidential data store list with encryption state and the privileged account inventory.
Pull every waiver and amendment case raised in the year from the case management tool.
Record extract timestamps, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent quarter-end populations of accounts, stores, privileged credentials and waiver cases exist with documented parameters.

testing.step: Reconcile the account population to HR and the application owners
actions: Match every human account to an active HRIS record and list orphans with no employee or contractor record.
Match the quarter's terminations from the HRIS to account disable timestamps and compute days between them.
Reconcile the system-extracted account counts to the certification campaign scope and explain any account excluded from certification.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every account ties to an HR record or is listed as an orphan, and certification scope differences are explained and signed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of privileged accounts, 100% of terminations in the quarter and 100% of waiver cases in the year.
Take 40 standard user entitlements at random using a recorded seed across at least four in-scope applications.
Take 100% of confidential data stores for the encryption check.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all privileged accounts, terminations, waivers and stores is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the MFA enforcement check on the sample
actions: Open the sign-on policy for each sampled application in the IAM platform and read the factor requirement rather than accepting the coverage report.
For each sampled account, open the user record and confirm an enrolled factor and its type, with phishing-resistant factors on administrators.
Attempt a documented read-only check for any bypass group or policy exclusion and list its members.
Any interactive account without an enrolled factor, or an undocumented bypass member, is an exception.
testing.done: MFA enforcement is verified from policy and user records, and every bypass exclusion is listed with its members.

testing.step: Verify encryption state and key rotation independently
actions: Query each sampled store's encryption metadata directly and record the algorithm, key source and last rotation date.
Compare the rotation date to the standard's interval and compute days overdue where applicable.
Test the external endpoint's TLS version and cipher suite and compare to the standard.
Log any store where the owner attestation asserts encryption the configuration does not show.
testing.done: each store's encryption and TLS state is independently queried and any contradiction with the owner attestation is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform certification decisions and trace revocations
actions: For each sampled entitlement, open the campaign record and confirm the reviewer was the manager or application owner and not the entitlement holder.
Check the decision was made before the day-30 close and is not a bulk approval applied in under a second per item.
For rejected entitlements, query the target system now and confirm the access is gone, with the removal evidence attached.
Any self-certification, post-close decision or surviving rejected entitlement is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled certification decision has an independent reviewer, a pre-close timestamp, and rejected access is confirmed removed.

testing.step: Recompute revocation and leaver service-level maths
actions: Recompute hours between each sampled termination effective date and the account disable timestamp and compare to the 24-hour standard.
Recompute business days between each certification rejection and the removal evidence timestamp against the 5-day standard.
Count breaches by system and by fulfilling team and quantify the maximum exposure window in days.
Confirm no leaver retained access into the following quarter.
testing.done: leaver and revocation timings are recomputed against their service levels with breaches counted by system and team.

testing.step: Test the code of ethics coverage, availability and waiver disclosure
actions: Read the published code and confirm it expressly covers the principal executive, principal financial and principal accounting officer or controller positions.
Open the URL named in the Form 10-K and confirm it resolves to the board-approved current version, dated.
For each waiver case, recompute business days from the deciding body's decision date to the 8-K filing or website posting and compare to the four-business-day limit.
Confirm the attestation roster shows every covered officer completed, and list any who did not.
testing.done: the code covers the named positions, the disclosed URL resolves to the approved version, and every waiver was disclosed within four business days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the account, store or case, the control that failed and the exposure window.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: unfederated application, bypass group misuse, bulk certification, HR feed failure, key rotation missed, or waiver not escalated same-day.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and route any undisclosed waiver to the General Counsel for a late-filing assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute exception rates by control against the zero-tolerance MFA, encryption and leaver thresholds and the 100% certification completion threshold.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, and assess whether any exception is a disclosure-controls deficiency for the 10-Q or 10-K.
Confirm the signer performed no sampled certification and administered no sampled account.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the exception rates and any disclosure-controls deficiency, with an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: CISO owns the annual incident response plan exercise and the incident record; the Corporate Secretary owns the Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing and the Ethics Officer owns the Item 5.05 route where an incident exposes a code of ethics waiver.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Form 8-K Item 1.05 and Item 5.05 instructions read on the SEC forms page, alongside Reg S-K Item 406, 17 CFR 229.406 and Regulation FD, 17 CFR 243.100, re-verified at each annual plan review and after each reportable event.

In-scope processes.value: Incident response lifecycle for cyber events touching policy administration, claims, billing and broker-facing systems — detection, triage, severity classification, materiality determination by the Disclosure Committee, regulator and policyholder notification, and post-incident review — plus the annual tabletop and technical exercise of that plan.

In-scope systems.value: Detection, case timeline and containment actions in the SIEM/SOAR; incident tickets and evidence in the security ticketing system; the materiality memo and the 8-K draft in the legal document repository.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Cyber Incident Response Plan with severity matrix, the Materiality Determination Procedure naming the Disclosure Committee as decider, the notification matrix (SEC Item 1.05, state insurance regulators, state attorneys general, affected policyholders, reinsurers) and the annual exercise procedure.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Plan approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and ratified by the Audit Committee annually; the materiality procedure approved by the General Counsel and reviewed after every Severity 1 event.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 8-K Item 1.05 due within four business days of the determination that an incident is material — the clock runs from the determination, which must itself be made without unreasonable delay; the annual exercise must complete before fiscal year end so the Item 106 description holds; annual certification of the plan is filed within 90 days after fiscal year end.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Opening a Severity 1 or 2 case pages the Disclosure Committee within 1 hour and starts a visible determination countdown; once materiality is determined the case shows a four-business-day filing countdown with alerts at 48, 24 and 8 hours remaining; the exercise task opens 120 days before fiscal year end.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exercise scenario, participant list, timeline and after-action report; incident case timelines, forensic reports, materiality memos, notification letters and filed 8-Ks retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository under legal hold where litigation is foreseeable.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed exercise, an unassessed Severity 1, a materiality determination delayed without documented reason, or a filing outside four business days is logged as an exception with owner, disposition and Audit Committee reporting date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs every materiality determination — positive or negative — and every after-action remediation item that touches the disclosure path.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every security incident case opened in the year at Severity 1 or 2, every materiality determination memo, every Form 8-K Item 1.05 filed or consciously not filed, and the annual exercise record with its after-action items.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any Severity 1 without a documented materiality determination, any determination-to-filing gap over four business days, or a fiscal year with no completed exercise is a fail; after-action items overdue beyond 90 days above 10% escalates to the Audit Committee.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual for the exercise and event-driven for notification; the test runs annually over the exercise and 100% of the year's Severity 1 and 2 cases, with an immediate post-event review after any Item 1.05 filing.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have participated in the exercise as a player or held a role on any sampled incident bridge.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual incident response assurance workpaper — exercise trace, case population, determination timing analysis, filing comparison and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: After-action report, incident case timeline, forensic summary, materiality memo, the filed Form 8-K Item 1.05 and the notification matrix showing which regulators were told and when, producible to an SEC comment letter or a state insurance department inquiry within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary answers SEC comments on Item 1.05 through EDGAR correspondence; the Regulatory Reporting Manager handles state insurance department notifications and follow-ups; the General Counsel clears every external statement, including any request for a national-security delay routed through the Attorney General.

checklist.step: Refresh the incident response plan and its severity matrix
actions: Review the plan against the year's real cases and update the severity matrix so a Severity 1 clearly captures material data loss, extended outage of the policy administration or claims platform, and ransomware.
Update the call tree with current names for the CISO, General Counsel, Corporate Secretary, Controller and the external forensics and breach-counsel retainers.
Add the SEC Item 1.05 determination step explicitly, with the Disclosure Committee named as decider, so nobody has to infer the disclosure path mid-incident.
Version the plan, publish it to the security SharePoint site and notify all responders of the change.
checklist.done: a versioned plan with a current call tree and an explicit Item 1.05 determination step is published and notified to responders.

checklist.step: Design the annual exercise scenario against a real threat
actions: Pick a scenario from the current threat library — for example ransomware encrypting the claims platform with exfiltration of claimant medical records.
Write the injects on a timeline: initial detection, spread to a second business unit, ransom note, journalist enquiry, and evidence that data was exfiltrated.
Define the objectives to be measured: time to declare, time to convene the Disclosure Committee, time to a materiality determination and time to a drafted 8-K.
Get the CISO and General Counsel to approve the scenario and the participant list before the date is booked.
checklist.done: an approved scenario with timed injects and measurable objectives, including a disclosure objective, exists before the exercise date.

checklist.step: Run the exercise with the full response and disclosure chain
actions: Convene the exercise on the booked date with SOC, IT, Claims, Underwriting Operations, Legal, Corporate Secretary, Communications and Investor Relations in the room or on the bridge.
Release the injects on the timeline and record wall-clock timestamps for each decision, not relative minutes.
Require the participants to actually draft the materiality memo and a skeleton 8-K Item 1.05 rather than describing what they would do.
Capture the chat and bridge transcript and the artifacts produced as exercise evidence.
checklist.done: the exercise ran with the full chain, timestamped decisions and a genuinely drafted materiality memo and 8-K skeleton.

checklist.step: Write the after-action report with owned, dated actions
actions: Report the measured times against the objectives and name each gap plainly — for example the Disclosure Committee could not be convened out of hours.
Raise one ticket per gap with a named owner and a committed date inside 90 days.
Route any gap touching the disclosure path to the General Counsel for sign-off on the fix.
Present the report to the Audit Committee and record the minutes reference.
checklist.done: an after-action report with measured times, a ticket per gap with owner and date, and an Audit Committee minutes reference.

checklist.step: Prove out-of-hours reachability of the decision chain
actions: Run an unannounced call-tree test outside business hours twice a year against the CISO, General Counsel, Corporate Secretary and CFO or their delegates.
Record acknowledgement times and any number that failed, and correct the roster the same week.
Confirm the on-call rotation in the ITSM platform matches the plan's call tree with no unfilled slots.
File the test results with the exercise evidence.
checklist.done: out-of-hours reachability is tested twice a year with recorded acknowledgement times and a corrected roster.

checklist.step: Detect and declare incidents against the severity matrix
actions: Triage each alert against the severity matrix and record the classification with the evidence that drove it in the case record.
Declare Severity 1 or 2 by paging the Incident Response Lead and opening the incident bridge within the plan's stated response time.
Start the case timeline immediately, logging detection time, declaration time and every containment action with a timestamp.
Notify the CISO and General Counsel of every Severity 1 or 2 within one hour of declaration, regardless of the hour.
checklist.done: each incident is classified with recorded evidence, declared within the plan's response time, and escalated to CISO and GC within one hour.

checklist.step: Contain, eradicate and preserve forensic evidence
actions: Isolate affected hosts through the endpoint platform and record the isolation timestamp per host.
Capture memory and disk images of the initial-access hosts before remediation and log the chain of custody for each image.
Preserve authentication, network flow and data-transfer logs beyond their normal retention by putting them on hold.
Hand the forensic timeline to the Incident Response Lead as the factual base for the materiality assessment.
checklist.done: affected hosts are isolated with timestamps, images and logs are preserved under chain of custody, and a forensic timeline is handed to the IR Lead.

checklist.step: Scope the data and policyholder impact
actions: Work with the application owners to identify which records were accessed or exfiltrated — policy numbers, claimant medical information, bank details, producer records.
Quantify affected individuals by state of residence, since that drives state notification thresholds and deadlines.
Record whether the data was encrypted at rest and whether keys were also compromised, as that changes several state safe harbours.
Give the quantified impact to the Disclosure Committee and to Claims and Policy Administration operational leads.
checklist.done: affected record types and counts by state of residence are quantified and handed to the Disclosure Committee.

checklist.step: Make and document the materiality determination without unreasonable delay
actions: Convene the Disclosure Committee as soon as the forensic and impact facts support a decision, and record why that date was the earliest reasonable one.

Assess materiality on the nature, scope and timing of the incident and its reasonably likely impact on financial condition and results, including claims-handling and underwriting disruption, not just record counts.
Write the determination memo — positive or negative — with the facts relied on, the members present and the exact date and time of the determination.
Sign the memo and file it in iManage; the signed date is the start of the four-business-day Item 1.05 clock where the determination is positive.
checklist.done: a signed, dated materiality memo exists for every Severity 1 with the reasoning and the determination timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: File the Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days
actions: Draft Item 1.05 describing the nature, scope and timing of the incident and its material impact or reasonably likely material impact, without technical detail that would impede response or remediation.
Have the General Counsel and external securities counsel clear the wording, and Investor Relations align any holding statement to it under Regulation FD.
Transmit through EDGAR within four business days of the determination date and record the accession number on the case.
Where facts are not yet determined, say so and calendar the Item 1.05 amendment within four business days of learning them.
checklist.done: the Item 1.05 8-K is filed within four business days of the determination, cleared by counsel, with the accession number on the case.

checklist.step: Work the wider regulator and counterparty notification matrix
actions: Notify the domiciliary insurance commissioner and every state where affected policyholders reside, using each state's cybersecurity event notification form and its 72-hour or 3-business-day clock where adopted.
Notify state attorneys general and consumer credit reporting agencies where the state breach statute requires it at the affected-resident count reached.
Notify reinsurers and any affected third-party administrator under the contractual notice clause and record the date sent.
Maintain a single notification matrix showing recipient, obligation source, due date, date sent and acknowledgement.
checklist.done: a notification matrix shows every regulator and counterparty notified against its own deadline, with acknowledgements recorded.

checklist.step: Control external and internal communications under Regulation FD
actions: Route all analyst and investor enquiries to the approved holding statement and refuse to give any detail not already in the 8-K.
Where any material non-public detail is disclosed selectively, file a Regulation FD 8-K promptly and no later than 24 hours or the start of the next trading day.
Brief the Contact Center Ops Manager with a policyholder-facing script so front-line answers do not exceed the filed disclosure.
Log every external statement made, by whom and when.
checklist.done: every external statement traces to the cleared holding statement and any selective disclosure is corrected by a Regulation FD filing.

checklist.step: Assess whether the incident exposed a code of ethics waiver
actions: Review the incident facts for any covered officer's departure from the code — for example an approved exception to the policy on handling confidential information.
Where an implicit waiver occurred, open a waiver case and route it to the deciding body the code names.
Notify the Corporate Secretary the same day so the Form 8-K Item 5.05 four-business-day clock is visible.
Record the outcome on the incident case so the disclosure package is complete.
checklist.done: any implicit code waiver arising from the incident is raised as a case, escalated the same day and disclosed or documented as not required.

checklist.step: Close the incident with a post-incident review and permanent fixes
actions: Hold the review within 15 business days of containment with responders, application owners and Legal present.
Record root cause, the control that failed, the detection gap, and the disclosure-path timings against the four-business-day requirement.
