Raise permanent-fix tickets with owners and dates, and feed the scenario back into the threat library and next year's exercise.
Report the incident, the disclosure treatment and the fixes to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: a post-incident review within 15 business days records root cause, disclosure timings and owned permanent fixes reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: File the annual certification and the evidence set
actions: Assemble the annual certification that the incident response plan was reviewed and exercised, signed by the CISO, and file it within 90 days after fiscal year end.
Move the exercise record, after-action report, incident cases, materiality memos, notification matrices and filed 8-Ks into the repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and set legal hold on any incident with foreseeable litigation or an open regulator inquiry.
Confirm the record is searchable by incident number, severity and filing accession number.
checklist.done: a signed annual certification is filed within 90 days of fiscal year end and the full incident evidence set is retained and searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents, determinations and exercise records
actions: Extract every security case opened in the fiscal year with severity, detection time, declaration time and closure time.
Extract independently from the SIEM the alerts that met Severity 1 or 2 criteria, so cases that were never opened become visible.
Pull every materiality memo from the legal repository and every Form 8-K filed in the year from the financial reporting repository.
Record extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent populations of cases, qualifying alerts, memos and filings exist with documented extract parameters.

testing.step: Reconcile declared incidents to the detection record
actions: Match each qualifying SIEM alert to an opened case and list alerts with no case.
For each unmatched alert, read the analyst disposition and judge it against the severity matrix rather than accepting the label.
List every case downgraded after opening and read the justification and who approved it.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every qualifying alert ties to a case or has a judged disposition, and downgrades are identified with their approvers.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Severity 1 cases, 100% of materiality memos and 100% of Item 1.05 filings.
Take 15 Severity 2 and downgraded cases at random using a recorded seed.
Take the full annual exercise record and its after-action ticket set.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Severity 1 cases, memos and filings is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the severity classification on the sample
actions: Read the case evidence for each sampled incident and apply the published severity matrix independently before reading the assigned severity.
Compare your classification to the recorded one and treat any downgrade that removed a disclosure assessment as an exception.
Check the declaration timestamp against the plan's response time for that severity.
Capture the case record and your classification note into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case carries an independent severity conclusion and any disclosure-removing downgrade is logged.

testing.step: Test the exercise actually happened as designed
actions: Compare the participant list on the after-action report to the calendar invitations and the bridge attendance log.
Confirm the disclosure objective was exercised by opening the drafted materiality memo and 8-K skeleton the exercise produced.
Check each measured time in the report against the timestamps in the exercise transcript.
Treat an exercise with no Legal or Corporate Secretary participation as a fail against the plan's own design.
testing.done: attendance, artifacts and measured times are verified against source records and the disclosure chain is confirmed to have participated.

testing.step: Recompute the determination and filing clocks
actions: For each sampled incident, compute elapsed days from the point the forensic and impact facts were known to the signed determination date and challenge any gap over a few days as unreasonable delay.
Compute business days from the determination timestamp to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp on the Item 1.05 filing, excluding weekends and federal holidays.
Compare each result to the four-business-day limit and record any breach in hours.
For amendments, recompute the four business days from the date the previously undetermined facts became known.
testing.done: determination and filing clocks are independently recomputed against the four-business-day limit with any breach quantified in hours.

testing.step: Trace the notification matrix to sent evidence
actions: For each sampled incident with policyholder impact, take the affected-resident counts by state and identify the notification obligations that triggered.
Open the submitted state cybersecurity event form or portal confirmation for each and compare the sent date to that state's deadline.
Confirm reinsurer and third-party administrator notices went out within the contractual notice period.
List any obligation identified but with no sent evidence as an exception.
testing.done: every triggered notification traces to a dated submission confirmation within its own deadline, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test after-action remediation closure
actions: Recompute days open for every after-action and post-incident ticket against the 90-day commitment.
Open the closure evidence on closed tickets and confirm it demonstrates the fix rather than asserting it.
Compute the percentage of after-action items overdue beyond 90 days and compare to the 10% threshold.
Check that repeat gaps from the prior year's report were closed rather than re-raised.
testing.done: after-action ageing is recomputed, closures are evidence-backed, and repeat gaps are identified against the prior year.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the incident number, the step that failed and the disclosure or notification consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: alert not case-opened, severity downgraded, committee not convened, determination delayed, filing late, or notification missed.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any late Item 1.05 filing to the General Counsel for a late-filing and Rule 12b-25 assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective against the zero-tolerance determination and filing thresholds.
Confirm the signer was not a player in the exercise and held no role on any sampled incident bridge.
Report the conclusion, any late filing and the exercise result to the Audit Committee at its next meeting.
File the signed workpaper with its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and any late determination or filing, with an Audit Committee reporting date recorded.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Corporate Secretary owns the annual certification package — the Item 408(b) insider trading policy disclosure, the Exhibit 19 policy filing and the officer certifications that accompany the Form 10-K; the Chief Info Security Officer countersigns the security-program element of the certification.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-K Item 408(b), 17 CFR 229.408(b), Exchange Act Section 13(a) and Rule 13a-1, 17 CFR 240.13a-1, and Rule 14a-3 with Schedule 14A read on eCFR before each 10-K drafting cycle, together with the SEC's Insider Trading Arrangements and Related Disclosures adopting release.

In-scope processes.value: Annual reporting cycle for the registrant and its insurance subsidiaries — insider trading policy administration and pre-clearance, Rule 10b5-1 plan adoption and tracking, Section 16 reporting, and the assembly and certification of the Form 10-K and the proxy statement disclosures.

In-scope systems.value: The 10-K and proxy drafts, exhibit index and certification signature pages in the financial reporting repository; the policy of record and pre-clearance decisions in iManage; the annual attestation roster in the learning management system.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Insider Trading Policy plus its administration procedure — covered-person definition, blackout calendar, pre-clearance workflow, Rule 10b5-1 cooling-off periods and the annual certification procedure covering who signs what, in which order, before the 10-K is transmitted.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Insider Trading Policy approved by the Board on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and re-approved annually; the certification procedure approved by the General Counsel and the Chief Financial Officer.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The Item 408(b) disclosure and Exhibit 19 policy filing go with the Form 10-K, and the Rule 13a-1 annual report and its Section 302 and 906 certifications are due within 90 days after fiscal year end for a non-accelerated filer; the proxy carrying the related disclosures is furnished no later than the date it is first sent to security holders.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Certification package tasks open at fiscal year end minus 45 days; sub-certification questionnaires issue at year end plus 10 days with a 15-day return; a hard alert fires at day 75 after year end if any certification signature page is still unsigned.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed sub-certification questionnaires, the executed Section 302 and 906 certifications, the board-approved insider trading policy versions, pre-clearance decisions, 10b5-1 plan records and the Exhibit 19 as filed, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A trade executed without pre-clearance, a 10b5-1 plan adopted inside a blackout or without the cooling-off period, a missing sub-certification, or a 10-K filed without Exhibit 19 is logged as an exception with owner, disposition and Audit Committee reporting date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every insider trading exception disposition and clears the Item 408(b) wording and the certification package before the Corporate Secretary releases the filing.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All covered persons under the insider trading policy during the fiscal year, every pre-clearance request and every trade by a Section 16 officer or director, every Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted, modified or terminated, and the full certification package supporting the Form 10-K.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any Section 16 trade without a pre-clearance record, any 10b5-1 plan adopted without the required cooling-off period, any sub-certification missing at the filing date, or a 10-K filed without the Item 408(b) disclosure and Exhibit 19, is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with the 90-day deadline; the test runs annually in the four weeks before the target filing date, with a quarterly interim check on pre-clearance and 10b5-1 records because trading is continuous.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside the Corporate Secretary's office and Legal and must not have administered any sampled pre-clearance or drafted any certification.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual certification and insider trading workpaper — covered-person roster, pre-clearance to trade reconciliation, 10b5-1 cooling-off recomputation, certification completeness matrix and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The filed Exhibit 19, the Item 408(b) disclosure, executed Section 302 and 906 certifications, the pre-clearance register and the 10b5-1 plan schedule, producible to an SEC comment letter or an enforcement inquiry within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary responds to SEC Division of Corporation Finance comments through EDGAR correspondence; the General Counsel handles any Division of Enforcement inquiry into insider trading and clears every response and any Rule 12b-25 late-filing notification.

checklist.step: Confirm the filer status that sets the 10-K deadline
actions: Compute public float as at the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter using the closing price and shares held by non-affiliates.
Apply the Rule 12b-2 definitions to set large accelerated, accelerated or non-accelerated status and record the resulting 60, 75 or 90-day deadline.
Tick the matching filer-status boxes on the 10-K cover page and confirm the smaller reporting company and emerging growth company answers agree.
Publish the target filing date to the Controller, Corporate Secretary and external auditor and load it into the close calendar.
checklist.done: filer status is computed from public float, the cover-page boxes match, and the resulting filing deadline is published to the reporting team.

checklist.step: Refresh and re-approve the insider trading policy
actions: Redline the policy against Item 408(b)'s expectation that it be reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws and the exchange listing standards.
Confirm it covers directors, officers, employees and the company's own transactions in its securities, since Item 408(b) asks about the company as well.
Take the redline to the Audit Committee for recommendation and to the Board for adoption, and capture the resolution date.
Version the adopted policy in iManage as the Exhibit 19 source document.
checklist.done: a board-adopted policy version exists that covers insiders and the company itself, versioned as the Exhibit 19 source.

checklist.step: Rebuild the covered-person roster and the blackout calendar
actions: Extract from the HRIS everyone in a role designated as covered — Section 16 officers, directors, finance, actuarial, reserving and investor relations staff — with effective dates.
Publish the blackout calendar for the year from the earnings release schedule, opening each window at the second business day after release and closing it two weeks before quarter end.
Notify additions and removals to the individuals concerned in writing and record the acknowledgement.
Reconcile the roster to the Section 16 filer list the Corporate Secretary maintains.
checklist.done: a reconciled covered-person roster and a published blackout calendar exist, with individual notifications acknowledged.

checklist.step: Operate pre-clearance for every insider transaction
actions: Require a pre-clearance request naming the security, transaction type, approximate size and intended date before any covered person trades.
Check the request against the blackout calendar and any event-specific blackout, and against the register of pending material non-public information.
Grant or refuse in writing with a validity window, typically five business days, and log the decision, decider and timestamp.
Refuse rather than condition where material non-public information exists, and record the reason without naming the information in the log.
checklist.done: every covered-person trade has a written pre-clearance decision with a timestamp and a stated validity window.

checklist.step: Administer Rule 10b5-1 plans against the cooling-off rules
actions: Record for each plan the adopting person, adoption date, first permitted trade date, duration, and whether the adopter is a director or officer.
Apply the cooling-off period: for directors and officers, the later of 90 days after adoption or two business days after the next periodic report, capped at 120 days; for others, 30 days.
Collect the director or officer representation as to awareness of material non-public information and good faith at adoption.
Track modifications as new adoptions restarting the cooling-off clock, and record terminations with dates.
checklist.done: each 10b5-1 plan has a recorded adoption date, computed first permitted trade date, and the required representation on file.

checklist.step: File Section 16 reports on time and reconcile them to the register
actions: File Form 4 within two business days of each reportable transaction and Form 3 within ten days of becoming an insider.
Tick the Rule 10b5-1(c) check-box on the Form 4 where the trade was made under a qualifying plan and record the plan adoption date in the footnote.
Reconcile every filed Form 4 to a pre-clearance record or an eligible 10b5-1 plan and investigate any trade with neither.
Sweep for Form 5 obligations before the 45-day post-year-end deadline.
checklist.done: every reportable transaction has a timely Form 4 with the correct 10b5-1 check-box and ties back to a pre-clearance or plan.

checklist.step: Collect the annual policy attestation from covered persons
actions: Assign the insider trading module and attestation to the full covered-person roster with a 30-day completion window after the policy is adopted.
Chase weekly and escalate incomplete Section 16 officers and directors to the General Counsel at day 21.
Export the completion roster with names, titles and dates as annual evidence.
Record any disclosed brokerage account or existing plan the attestation surfaces and add it to the monitoring list.
checklist.done: the attestation roster shows every covered person completed within 30 days, with disclosed accounts and plans added to monitoring.

checklist.step: Issue and collect the sub-certification questionnaires
actions: Issue sub-certifications at year end plus 10 days to business unit heads, the CISO, the Chief Actuary, the General Counsel and the heads of Claims, Underwriting and Investments.
Ask each to confirm the completeness of disclosures, known control deficiencies, litigation and regulatory matters, and any known fraud, with a 15-day return.
Read every qualified answer and open a follow-up item with the signer rather than accepting a caveat into the file.
Track the completeness matrix daily from day 60 and escalate any gap at day 75.
checklist.done: every required sub-certification is returned and signed, with each qualified answer followed up and dispositioned.

checklist.step: Assemble the disclosure package and the Item 408(b) narrative
actions: Draft the Item 408(b) statement saying whether the company has adopted insider trading policies and procedures, describing them at a level that matches the filed policy, or explaining why not.
Add the policy to the exhibit index as Exhibit 19 and confirm it renders in the EDGAR submission preview.
Draft the Item 408(a) quarterly disclosure of any director or officer 10b5-1 or non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement adopted, modified or terminated, with the material terms other than pricing.
Cross-check the narrative against the pre-clearance register and the plan schedule so nothing described is contradicted by the records.
checklist.done: the Item 408(a) and 408(b) disclosures are drafted, Exhibit 19 is in the index, and the narrative agrees with the plan and pre-clearance records.

checklist.step: Run the disclosure controls evaluation supporting the certifications
actions: Assemble the results of control testing for the year, including the access and security controls the CISO certifies to, and list all identified deficiencies.
Aggregate deficiencies and conclude on significant deficiencies and material weaknesses with the Controller and the external auditor.
Prepare the Rule 13a-15 conclusion on the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period.
Present the conclusion and the deficiency list to the Disclosure Committee and the Audit Committee before signature.
checklist.done: a documented disclosure-controls conclusion with an aggregated deficiency list is presented to the Disclosure and Audit Committees.

checklist.step: Execute the Section 302 and 906 certifications
actions: Review the final 10-K text, the sub-certification file and the disclosure-controls conclusion before signing.
Sign the Section 302 certifications as Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 with the CEO, using the exact prescribed wording without modification.
Sign the Section 906 certification furnished as Exhibit 32 and confirm it is furnished rather than filed.
Confirm the signature dates equal the filing date, since a certification dated before the final document is a defect.
checklist.done: Exhibits 31.1, 31.2 and 32 are executed in the prescribed wording with signature dates equal to the filing date.

checklist.step: Countersign the security-program element of the certification
actions: Confirm from the GRC platform that the annual security program review, the risk assessment and the incident response exercise all completed in the fiscal year.
List any open critical finding that could bear on the disclosure-controls conclusion and give it to the SOX Program Manager.
Sign the CISO sub-certification covering the accuracy of the security disclosures and the operation of the certified controls.
File the signed sub-certification with the certification package.
checklist.done: a signed CISO sub-certification is in the package, with open critical findings disclosed to the SOX Program Manager.

checklist.step: Transmit the annual report within the filer-status deadline
actions: Validate the EDGAR submission — exhibit index, Inline XBRL tagging, cover-page tags and the signature page — and clear every validation warning before transmission.
Transmit on or before the 90-day deadline after fiscal year end and record the accession number and acceptance timestamp.
Where the deadline cannot be met, file Form 12b-25 by the business day after the due date and complete the filing inside the 15-day extension.
Post the filed report to the investor relations site the same day and notify Investor Relations.
checklist.done: the Form 10-K is accepted on EDGAR within the deadline with its accession number recorded, or a Form 12b-25 was filed on time.

checklist.step: Furnish the proxy disclosures no later than first delivery to holders
actions: Confirm the Schedule 14A carries the annual report or the Rule 14a-3(b) annual report to security holders as required.
File the definitive proxy on EDGAR no later than the date the proxy materials are first sent or given to security holders.
Check the say-on-pay and say-on-frequency resolutions required by Rule 14a-21 appear where due.
Record the mailing date and the EDGAR accession number together in the filing log.
checklist.done: the definitive proxy is filed no later than first delivery to holders, with mailing date and accession number logged.

checklist.step: Retain the certification package under the retention label
actions: Move the sub-certifications, executed certifications, adopted policy version, pre-clearance register, plan schedule and attestation roster into the repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and legal hold on anything connected to an open inquiry or restatement.
Confirm the record is searchable by fiscal year, signer name and accession number.
Give the external auditor read access to the package for the year-end file.
checklist.done: the certification package is filed under a 7-year label, searchable by signer and accession number, and available to the auditor.

testing.step: Build the population of covered persons, trades, plans and certifications
actions: Extract the covered-person roster with effective dates independently from the HRIS and the Section 16 filer list.
Pull every Form 3, 4 and 5 filed for the company on EDGAR during the fiscal year with transaction dates and check-box states.
Pull the pre-clearance register, the 10b5-1 plan schedule and the full certification package from their systems of record.
Record extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent populations of covered persons, Section 16 filings, pre-clearances, plans and certifications exist with documented parameters.

testing.step: Reconcile filed insider transactions to pre-clearances and plans
actions: Match every Form 4 transaction to a pre-clearance decision covering that date and security, or to an eligible 10b5-1 plan.
List transactions with neither as automatic exceptions and quantify the shares and value involved.
Check the Rule 10b5-1(c) check-box state on each Form 4 against the plan schedule and flag mismatches.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every insider transaction reconciles to a pre-clearance or an eligible plan, with mismatched check-boxes flagged and the reconciliation signed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Section 16 officer and director transactions and 100% of 10b5-1 plans adopted, modified or terminated in the year.
Take 25 non-Section 16 covered-person pre-clearance requests at random using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of required sub-certifications for the completeness test.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all insider transactions, all plans and all sub-certifications is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Recompute the 10b5-1 cooling-off periods
actions: For each director or officer plan, recompute the first permitted trade date as the later of 90 days after adoption or two business days after the periodic report for the quarter of adoption, capped at 120 days.
For other covered persons, recompute the 30-day period from adoption.
Compare the first actual trade under the plan to the recomputed date and record any trade inside the cooling-off period in days.
Confirm a modification was treated as a new adoption restarting the clock rather than a continuation.
testing.done: every plan's cooling-off period is independently recomputed and any trade inside it is quantified in days.

testing.step: Re-perform the pre-clearance judgement on the sample
actions: For each sampled request, read the decision date against the published blackout calendar and any event-specific blackout in force.
Reach an independent grant or refuse conclusion before reading the recorded decision.
Treat a clearance granted inside a blackout, or a trade executed outside the stated validity window, as an exception.
Capture the register entry and your conclusion note into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled pre-clearance has an independent conclusion and any blackout or validity-window breach is logged.

testing.step: Trace the Item 408 disclosures and Exhibit 19 to the filing
actions: Open the filed Form 10-K on EDGAR and confirm Exhibit 19 is present and opens to the board-adopted policy version, dated.
Read the Item 408(b) statement and check every descriptive claim against the policy text and the pre-clearance register.
Check each quarterly Item 408(a) disclosure against the plan schedule for adoptions, modifications and terminations by directors and officers.
Log any plan in the schedule with no corresponding Item 408(a) disclosure as an exception.
testing.done: Exhibit 19 matches the adopted policy and every plan event in the schedule appears in an Item 408(a) disclosure.

testing.step: Test certification completeness and signature dating
actions: Compare the sub-certification completeness matrix to the required signer list and list any missing return.
Open Exhibits 31.1, 31.2 and 32 as filed and compare the wording character by character to the prescribed form — any alteration is a defect.
Compare each signature date to the filing date and flag any certification signed before the final document was assembled.
Read every qualified sub-certification answer and confirm a documented follow-up disposition exists.
testing.done: all required sub-certifications are present, the filed certifications use unaltered prescribed wording, and dates equal the filing date.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and the actual filing date
actions: Recompute public float independently from the closing price and non-affiliate share count at the last business day of the second fiscal quarter.
Derive the filer status and the 60, 75 or 90-day deadline and compare it to the cover-page boxes.
Compare the EDGAR acceptance timestamp to the derived deadline and record any overrun in days.
Where a Form 12b-25 was used, confirm it was filed by the business day after the due date and the filing landed inside the 15-day extension.
testing.done: filer status and the deadline are independently derived and the actual acceptance date is compared, with any overrun quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the person, transaction or certification, the requirement missed and the exposure.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: roster gap, blackout not enforced, cooling-off miscomputed, check-box error, sub-certification not chased, or exhibit omitted.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any unpre-cleared Section 16 trade to the General Counsel for an enforcement-risk assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective against the zero-tolerance pre-clearance, cooling-off and certification thresholds.
Confirm the signer administered no sampled pre-clearance and drafted no part of the certification package.
Report the conclusion, any unpre-cleared trade and any certification defect to the Audit Committee at its next meeting.
File the signed workpaper with its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rate, with an Audit Committee reporting date recorded.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Third-Party Risk Manager owns per-vendor security due diligence and the annual re-assessment cycle; the Ethics Officer owns extension of the code of ethics and its waiver reporting to vendor-facing conduct, and the Corporate Secretary files any Form 8-K Item 5.05 that results.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-K Item 406, 17 CFR 229.406 and Regulation FD, 17 CFR 243.100 read on eCFR, plus Reg S-K Item 106(b)(1)(v) on processes for oversight of risks from third-party service providers, re-verified before each 10-K drafting cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Vendor lifecycle for third parties touching policyholder, claimant, producer or financial-reporting data — sourcing and due diligence, contract security and audit-rights clauses, onboarding, annual re-assessment, incident and subcontractor notification, and termination with data return or destruction.

In-scope systems.value: Vendor master, sourcing events and purchase orders in the procurement platform; executed contracts and clause data in Icertis CLM; assessment records, risk tiers and findings in Archer GRC.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third-Party Risk Management Standard — inherent-risk tiering by data class and criticality, the due-diligence question set per tier, mandatory contract clauses, the annual re-assessment cadence, the finding remediation service levels, and the vendor code of conduct acknowledgement requirement.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and the Procurement Manager, ratified by the Operational Risk Committee, and reviewed annually or on any material change to the outsourcing footprint.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Due diligence must close before contract signature and before any data is transferred; critical and high-tier vendors are re-assessed annually on the contract anniversary; the third-party oversight description is filed with the Form 10-K within the filer-status deadline, and any vendor-related code of ethics waiver goes on Form 8-K Item 5.05 within four business days.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Re-assessment tasks open 90 days before each contract anniversary with reminders at 60, 30 and 10 days; assurance-report expiry alerts fire 45 days before a SOC 2 report period lapses; a contract-signature gate blocks purchase order release while due diligence is open.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Due-diligence questionnaires, SOC 2 Type II reports and bridge letters, penetration-test summaries, executed contracts with the security schedule, assessment scores, finding tickets and termination data-destruction certificates retained 7 years after contract end in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Data transferred before diligence closed, a contract without the security schedule or audit rights, a lapsed assurance report on a critical vendor, or an overdue vendor finding is logged as an exception with owner, disposition and Operational Risk Committee reporting date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CISO signs every risk acceptance that lets a vendor operate with an open high or critical finding, and every approval to onboard a vendor whose assurance report is unavailable.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All active third parties in the vendor master that process, store or transmit company or policyholder data during the fiscal year, every new vendor onboarded in the year, every re-assessment due in the year, and every vendor-related code of ethics waiver.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any critical or high-tier vendor with data access and no completed diligence, no executed security schedule, or no assurance report covering the fiscal year is a fail; overdue re-assessments above 5% of the due population escalates to the Operational Risk Committee.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-vendor at onboarding and annual thereafter; the test runs annually over the full critical and high-tier population plus a quarterly interim check on new onboardings, since new vendors are where diligence is skipped.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Procurement and Third-Party Risk and must not have scored or approved any sampled vendor assessment.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual third-party oversight workpaper — vendor master reconciliation, onboarding gate testing, assurance-report coverage analysis, contract clause trace and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Vendor inventory by risk tier, the due-diligence file and assurance report for each critical vendor, executed security schedules, the finding ageing report and the Item 106 third-party oversight description, producible to an SEC comment letter or a state insurance department outsourcing enquiry within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary answers SEC comments on the third-party oversight disclosure; the Regulatory Reporting Manager answers state insurance department questions on outsourcing arrangements; the General Counsel clears every response and any statement about a vendor incident.

checklist.step: Rebuild the inventory of third parties that touch company data
actions: Export the active vendor master with spend, contract owner and category, and filter to vendors paid in the fiscal year.
Ask each business owner to confirm whether the vendor processes, stores or transmits policyholder, claimant, producer or financial-reporting data, and through which system.
Add third parties reached outside procurement — SaaS subscriptions on corporate cards, data providers and broker-facing integrations — by reconciling to the CMDB and the expense feed.
Publish the in-scope inventory and have the Third-Party Risk Manager approve it as the assessment population.
checklist.done: an approved in-scope vendor inventory exists, reconciled to spend and the CMDB, with the data touched named per vendor.

checklist.step: Tier each vendor by inherent risk
actions: Score each vendor on data class handled, record volume, system connectivity, whether it can initiate payments, and business criticality if unavailable.
Assign critical, high, medium or low tier from the published matrix and record the driving factor for each.
Mark vendors that would trigger a policyholder notification if breached — third-party administrators, print and mail, medical bill review, salvage vendors.
Have the business owner confirm the tier and record any challenge and its resolution.
checklist.done: every in-scope vendor carries an evidenced risk tier with a named driving factor and business-owner confirmation.

checklist.step: Run due diligence before any contract is signed
actions: Issue the tier-appropriate question set covering access control and MFA, encryption at rest and in transit, secure development, logging and monitoring, backup and recovery, and subcontractor use.
Request the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate and the latest external penetration-test summary, and check the report period actually covers the last twelve months.
Read the SOC 2 exceptions and the complementary user entity controls, and list which of those controls the company must itself operate.
Score the assessment, record findings with severity, and give a written go, go-with-conditions or no-go to Procurement.
checklist.done: a scored diligence file with the assurance report, its exceptions and a written go/no-go decision exists before contract signature.

checklist.step: Put the mandatory security and audit clauses into the contract
actions: Attach the standard information security schedule setting encryption, access control, personnel screening and secure disposal obligations.

Include incident notification within 24 hours of the vendor becoming aware, audit and assessment rights, subcontractor approval, data return or destruction on termination, and the right to terminate for security failure.
Where the vendor rejects a clause, log the deviation with the business justification and route it to the CISO for acceptance before signature.
Tag the executed contract in the CLM with the clause set present so contract-level reporting is possible without reading PDFs.
checklist.done: the executed contract carries the security schedule and audit rights, with every deviation logged and CISO-accepted.

checklist.step: Gate onboarding and data transfer on a closed diligence file
actions: Configure the sourcing workflow so a purchase order for an in-scope category cannot release while the diligence record is open.
Require the assessment reference number on the requisition and validate it against the GRC record.
Block the data-transfer or integration request in the ITSM queue until the assessment shows go or go-with-conditions.
Report any override, who approved it and why, to the Operational Risk Committee monthly.
checklist.done: no purchase order or data transfer for an in-scope vendor releases without a closed diligence record, and overrides are reported monthly.

checklist.step: Extend the code of conduct and ethics obligations to the vendor
actions: Send the supplier code of conduct with the contract and collect a signed acknowledgement from an authorised vendor officer.
Include the anti-bribery, conflicts-of-interest, confidential-information and gift-and-entertainment provisions that mirror the company code applicable to its senior financial officers.
Record any vendor relationship involving a covered officer's family member or financial interest, and route it as a potential code waiver case.
Notify the Corporate Secretary the same day any such case is opened so the four-business-day Form 8-K Item 5.05 clock is visible.
checklist.done: every in-scope vendor has a signed supplier code acknowledgement and any covered-officer conflict is raised as a waiver case the same day.

checklist.step: Onboard the vendor into monitoring and access control
actions: Create vendor user accounts through the standard joiner process with MFA enforced and a named internal sponsor per account.
Set an account expiry equal to the contract end date so dormant vendor access cannot outlive the engagement.
Add the vendor's accounts to the quarterly access certification campaign scope with the sponsor as reviewer.
Register the vendor's connectivity — IP ranges, API credentials, file transfer accounts — with the network and integration teams.
checklist.done: vendor accounts exist with MFA, a named sponsor, a contract-dated expiry and inclusion in the quarterly certification.

checklist.step: Track assurance report currency across the portfolio
actions: Record each vendor's SOC 2 report period end and set an alert 45 days before the gap between the period end and today reaches three months.
Request a bridge letter covering the gap between the report period end and the current date for every critical vendor.
Read each new report's opinion type and exceptions, and open findings for exceptions relevant to the services the company buys.
Report portfolio coverage — percentage of critical vendors with a current report — to the CISO monthly.
checklist.done: every critical vendor has a current assurance report or bridge letter, with portfolio coverage reported to the CISO monthly.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-assessment on the contract anniversary
actions: Open the re-assessment 90 days before the anniversary and re-confirm the data classes and volumes actually processed, since scope creeps quietly.
Re-issue the tier-appropriate question set, refresh the assurance report and re-score the vendor.
Compare the new score to last year's and investigate any material improvement claimed without evidence.
Re-tier the vendor where scope has changed and update the contract obligations accordingly.
checklist.done: each critical and high-tier vendor is re-scored on or before its anniversary with data scope re-confirmed and tier updated.

checklist.step: Drive vendor findings to closure against service levels
actions: Raise a finding per gap with the vendor contact, the internal business owner, the severity and a committed remediation date — 30 days critical, 90 days high.
Require vendor-supplied evidence of the fix, not a status email, before closing.
Escalate overdue critical findings to the vendor's executive sponsor and to the internal business owner at day 45.
Where a finding cannot be fixed, route a risk acceptance with compensating controls to the CISO for signature.
checklist.done: each vendor finding has an owner and a committed date, closes on vendor evidence, or carries a CISO-signed acceptance.

checklist.step: Wire vendor incident and subcontractor notification into the response plan
actions: Give each critical vendor the 24-hour security incident notification address and confirm they have tested it at least once.
Require notification of any new subcontractor with data access at least 30 days before it is engaged, and re-assess the subcontractor before approval.
On any vendor incident notice, open an internal case immediately so the company's own materiality and state notification clocks start.
Test the vendor notification path annually as part of the incident response exercise.
checklist.done: critical vendors have a tested 24-hour notification path and subcontractor changes are notified 30 days ahead and re-assessed.

checklist.step: Terminate cleanly with data return or destruction
actions: On termination or expiry, issue the data return and destruction instruction referencing the contract clause and the format required.
Collect a signed certificate of destruction naming the systems, backups and date, and file it against the contract record.
Disable all vendor accounts and network connectivity on the termination date and confirm removal with the IAM and network teams.
Close the vendor record in the GRC platform only when the certificate and the access-removal confirmation are both attached.
checklist.done: every terminated vendor has a signed destruction certificate and confirmed access removal before its record is closed.

checklist.step: Report portfolio risk to the Operational Risk Committee
actions: Prepare a quarterly pack showing vendor counts by tier, assessments overdue, assurance-report coverage, open findings by severity and age, and accepted risks.
Name the business owners behind the overdue and the accepted items rather than reporting totals only.
Record the committee's directions and convert each into a tracked action with an owner and a date.
Feed the same metrics to the CISO for the Item 106 third-party oversight description.
checklist.done: a quarterly portfolio pack with named owners is minuted at the Operational Risk Committee and feeds the Item 106 description.

checklist.step: Support the third-party oversight statements in the annual report
actions: Give the Corporate Secretary the artifacts behind each third-party oversight sentence in the Item 106 disclosure — the standard, the tiering matrix, coverage metrics and the committee minutes.
Confirm the disclosure does not claim a process the portfolio metrics contradict, such as full annual re-assessment when re-assessments are overdue.
Sign the sub-certification covering the accuracy of the third-party oversight statements.
Archive the support set against the filing accession number.
checklist.done: each third-party oversight statement in the filing maps to a named artifact and is covered by a signed CISO sub-certification.

checklist.step: Retain the vendor evidence set under the retention label
actions: Move diligence files, assurance reports and bridge letters, executed contracts with the security schedule, finding tickets and destruction certificates into the repository under the vendor and contract year.
Apply the retention label of 7 years after contract end and set legal hold on any vendor connected to an incident or dispute.
Confirm the record is searchable by vendor name, risk tier and contract number.
Give Internal Audit read access ahead of the annual test.
checklist.done: vendor evidence is filed under a 7-years-after-contract-end label, searchable by vendor, tier and contract number.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope vendors, onboardings and assessments
actions: Extract the full vendor master with fiscal-year spend independently of the in-scope inventory Third-Party Risk produced.
Extract new vendor records created in the year and all assessments due, started and completed from Archer.
Pull the CMDB integration list and the SaaS discovery report so vendors reached outside procurement appear.
Record extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent populations of vendors, onboardings and assessments exist, including vendors reached outside procurement.

testing.step: Reconcile the in-scope inventory to spend and system connectivity
actions: Match every vendor with fiscal-year spend to an in-scope or out-of-scope determination and read the rationale for each exclusion.
Match every external integration in the CMDB and every SaaS application in the discovery report to a vendor record.
List vendors with data access that never entered the third-party risk process as automatic exceptions.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every paid vendor and every external integration ties to a scope determination, with unassessed data-access vendors listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of critical-tier vendors and 100% of vendors onboarded in the year with data access.
Take 20 high and medium-tier vendors at random using a recorded seed.
Take 100% of terminations in the year for the data-destruction test.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all critical vendors, all new data-access onboardings and all terminations is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the risk tiering on the sample
actions: Read the vendor's actual service description, data flows and contract scope, then apply the published tiering matrix independently.
Compare to the recorded tier and treat any under-tiering that reduced the diligence question set as an exception.
Check the tier against the data volumes reported by the business owner rather than the volumes assumed at onboarding.
Capture the tiering record and your conclusion into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled vendor has an independent tier conclusion and any under-tiering that weakened diligence is logged.

testing.step: Test the onboarding gate against the data-transfer date
actions: For each sampled onboarding, compare the diligence completion date to the contract signature date and to the first data transfer or integration go-live date.
Any data transferred before the diligence closed is an exception regardless of the eventual assessment outcome.
Read the override record where the gate was bypassed and confirm a CISO approval exists and pre-dates the transfer.
Quantify the exposure window in days for each breach.
testing.done: diligence completion pre-dates contract signature and first data transfer for every sampled onboarding, or the breach is quantified.

testing.step: Trace the mandatory contract clauses to the executed agreement
actions: Open the executed contract for each sampled vendor and locate the information security schedule, the incident notification clause with its hour count, audit rights, subcontractor approval and the data return or destruction clause.
Compare the notification period in the contract to the 24-hour standard and record any longer period agreed.
Confirm every clause deviation carries a logged justification and a CISO acceptance dated before signature.
Do not accept the CLM clause tag as evidence — read the executed document.
testing.done: each mandatory clause is located in the executed document, with deviations carrying dated CISO acceptances.

testing.step: Test assurance report coverage and exception handling
actions: For each sampled vendor, open the SOC 2 Type II report and confirm the examination period covers the fiscal year, with a bridge letter for any gap over three months.
Read the opinion type and reject qualified opinions accepted without a documented assessment of the qualification.
Check that each report exception relevant to the purchased services became a tracked finding.
Confirm the complementary user entity controls the report lists are assigned to an internal owner and tested.
testing.done: every sampled vendor has period-covering assurance with exceptions tracked and user entity controls assigned internally.

testing.step: Recompute re-assessment and finding ageing
actions: Recompute the re-assessment due date as the contract anniversary and compare it to the completion date, recording days overdue.
Compute the percentage of the due population completed late and compare to the 5% threshold.
Recompute days open on every sampled vendor finding against the 30 and 90-day service levels.
Confirm each closed finding has vendor-supplied evidence attached rather than a status assertion.
testing.done: re-assessment and finding ageing are independently recomputed against their thresholds with closures evidence-backed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the vendor, contract number, the control that failed and the data exposed.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: vendor outside procurement, gate overridden, tier understated, assurance lapsed, clause omitted, or destruction certificate missing.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any unassessed critical vendor to the CISO for an immediate risk decision.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective against the zero-tolerance diligence and assurance thresholds and the 5% overdue limit.
Confirm the signer scored and approved no sampled vendor assessment.
Report the conclusion, unassessed critical vendors and the overdue rate to the Operational Risk Committee and the Audit Committee.
File the signed workpaper with its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and overdue rate, with both committees given a recorded reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns preparation of the GAAP financial statements and schedules in Regulation S-X form for the Form 10-K and 10-Q; the Statutory Reporting Manager owns the parallel NAIC annual and quarterly statement blanks for each insurance subsidiary and reconciles them to GAAP.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Regulation S-X, 17 CFR Part 210 (including Article 7 for insurance companies and Rules 5-04 and 7-05 on schedules), Rule 14a-3(b) and Rule 13a-13 read on eCFR before each reporting cycle, alongside the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual.

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual close for the registrant and every insurance subsidiary — general ledger close, reserve booking, investment valuation, reinsurance accounting, consolidation, statutory-to-GAAP bridging, Regulation S-X schedule preparation and the audited financial statements included in the Form 10-K.

In-scope systems.value: General ledger and subledgers in SAP S/4HANA, account reconciliations and close tasks in BlackLine, consolidation and eliminations in the close tool, statutory blanks in the NAIC statutory reporting application, and the tagged filing in the financial reporting repository.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Financial Close and External Reporting Procedure — close calendar by legal entity, account reconciliation standard, reserve and investment valuation sign-offs, the statutory-to-GAAP bridge method, the Regulation S-X schedule preparation instructions and the Inline XBRL tagging review.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer, reviewed annually and on any change to the NAIC blanks, an S-X amendment or a new accounting standard adoption; the Audit Committee approves the external auditor's scope each year.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: NAIC quarterly statement due 45 days after quarter end and the annual statement by 1 March, with the audited statutory statements by 1 June; the Form 10-Q under Rule 13a-13 is due within 45 days of quarter end and the Form 10-K with the S-X-compliant audited statements within 90 days after fiscal year end for a non-accelerated filer.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar tasks alert at day 3, 6 and 9 of the close; a statutory blank alert fires at quarter end plus 30 days and at 15 February for the annual statement; a filing-readiness gate at day 75 after year end reports any unsigned reconciliation or open audit item.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Trial balances, signed account reconciliations, journal entry support, actuarial reserve memoranda, investment valuation files, statutory-to-GAAP bridges, the S-X schedules and the auditor's report retained 7 years in the financial reporting repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Unreconciled accounts past the close deadline, unsupported journal entries, a required S-X schedule omitted or a statutory blank filed late are logged as exceptions with owner, disposition and the Audit Committee meeting at which they were reported.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the close package and any out-of-period adjustment; the Appointed Actuary signs the reserve opinion supporting the statutory statements before either filing is released.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All balance sheet accounts requiring reconciliation at each period end across every reporting entity, all manual and top-side journal entries posted in the close, every Regulation S-X schedule required for the filing, and every NAIC quarterly and annual blank filed in the year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A fail is any account reconciliation unsigned at filing, any top-side entry without support, any required S-X schedule omitted, any statutory blank filed after its statutory due date, or a statutory-to-GAAP bridge that does not tie; unreconciled balances above the clearly trivial threshold of $250,000 escalate to the CFO.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly and annual; the test runs each quarter over that quarter's close and filing population, with an expanded annual pass covering the S-X schedules, the audited statements and the statutory annual statement.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Financial Reporting and Statutory Reporting and must not have prepared or approved any sampled reconciliation, entry or schedule.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly close and reporting workpaper — reconciliation completeness extract, journal entry sample and support, schedule trace, statutory-to-GAAP bridge recomputation and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the SOX binder.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed reconciliations, the close package, S-X schedules with their supporting workpapers, the auditor's report, the statutory blanks with their jurat pages and the actuarial opinion, producible to an SEC comment letter or a state financial examination within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Controller drafts responses to SEC comments on the financial statements and schedules with the external auditor consulted; the Statutory Reporting Manager answers state insurance department and NAIC data-quality queries; the CFO and General Counsel clear every response before submission.

checklist.step: Publish the close calendar and lock the reporting entity scope
actions: List every reporting entity — the registrant, each insurance subsidiary with its NAIC company code, and non-insurance affiliates — with its statutory domicile and reporting basis.
Publish the close calendar in BlackLine with task owners, dependencies and day numbers, ending at the 10-Q filing on day 45 and the 10-K on day 90.
Confirm the materiality and clearly trivial thresholds with the external auditor and record them at the top of the calendar.
Circulate the calendar to Actuarial, Investments, Reinsurance, Tax and each subsidiary controller and record their acceptance.
checklist.done: a published close calendar names every reporting entity, task owner and day number and is accepted by all contributing functions.

checklist.step: Close the subledgers and confirm the interfaces to the general ledger
actions: Close premium, claims, billing, investment and payroll subledgers in sequence and confirm each posting run completed with no error queue.
Reconcile each subledger control total to the general ledger account balance and investigate every difference above the clearly trivial threshold.
Confirm the policy administration and claims platform feeds posted the full period, using record counts and control totals from the source system owners.
Lock the period in the general ledger once interfaces agree and record the lock timestamp.
checklist.done: every subledger ties to its control account, all interface feeds are confirmed complete, and the period is locked with a timestamp.

checklist.step: Book actuarial reserves with the supporting memorandum
actions: Run the reserve analysis by line and accident year and produce the indicated range and the selected point estimate.
Write the reserve memorandum recording method changes, assumption changes and the reason for any selection away from the indication.
Give the Controller the booking entry by legal entity, line and gross, ceded and net split, plus the unallocated loss adjustment expense provision.
Have the Chief Actuary review and sign the memorandum before the entry is posted.
checklist.done: reserves are posted from a signed memorandum that documents the selection, method and assumption changes by entity and line.

checklist.step: Value investments and record impairments
actions: Take month-end prices from the primary pricing source, apply the pricing hierarchy for level 2 and 3 securities and document every price challenge and its resolution.
Produce the fair value hierarchy table by asset class for the S-X and ASC 820 disclosures.
Run the credit loss and other-than-temporary impairment analysis and give the Controller the entries with the security-level support.
Reconcile the custodian position and cash statements to the investment subledger and clear breaks before the ledger closes.
checklist.done: investments are valued from a documented hierarchy, custodian positions reconcile, and impairment entries carry security-level support.

checklist.step: Settle reinsurance balances and record the recoverable
actions: Calculate ceded premium, ceded losses and commission by treaty for the period and issue the accounts to each reinsurer.
Age the reinsurance recoverable by reinsurer and compute the allowance for uncollectible amounts using the counterparty rating and any collateral held.
Confirm the collateral position — letters of credit and trust balances — with Treasury for any unauthorised reinsurer, since it drives the statutory credit.
Give the Controller the entries and the recoverable schedule that supports the S-X and statutory disclosures.
checklist.done: ceded balances are settled by treaty, the recoverable is aged with an allowance, and collateral is confirmed for unauthorised reinsurers.

checklist.step: Complete and sign every balance sheet reconciliation
actions: Prepare each assigned reconciliation in BlackLine with the source of the supporting balance attached, not a screenshot of the ledger itself.
Age every reconciling item and give each one over 60 days an owner and a clearance date.
Submit for preparer and reviewer sign-off within the calendar day set for the account's risk rating.
Escalate any account that cannot be reconciled to the Controller before day 9 rather than filing it unreconciled.
checklist.done: every balance sheet account has a signed preparer and reviewer reconciliation with aged items owned and dated.

checklist.step: Control manual and top-side journal entries
actions: Require a written business reason, calculation support and an independent approver on every manual entry above the posting threshold.
Review the top-side and consolidation entry listing daily during the close, questioning any entry that moves income without a subledger source.
Confirm no entry was posted by its own approver by running the segregation report from the general ledger.
Sign the entry log at the close of the period.
checklist.done: every manual and top-side entry carries support, an independent approver and appears on a Controller-signed entry log.

checklist.step: Consolidate and eliminate intercompany balances
actions: Load each entity's trial balance into the consolidation tool and confirm the load control totals match the source ledgers.
Match intercompany balances by partner and clear differences with the counterparty entity controller before elimination.
Post eliminations for intercompany reinsurance, service agreements and investments in subsidiaries and confirm the consolidated balance sheet balances.
Produce the consolidated trial balance and hand it to Financial Reporting with the elimination support.
checklist.done: the consolidation loads tie to source ledgers, intercompany balances clear, and the consolidated trial balance balances with elimination support.

checklist.step: Prepare the NAIC quarterly and annual statement blanks
actions: Map the statutory trial balance into the current-year blank for each insurance subsidiary, populating the assets, liabilities, summary of operations, cash flow, Schedule P, Schedule F and Schedule D exhibits.
Run the NAIC cross-check edits and clear every failing edit rather than filing with an explanation where a correction is possible.
Obtain the Appointed Actuary's Statement of Actuarial Opinion and attach it to the annual statement.
Submit the quarterly blank within 45 days of quarter end and the annual blank by 1 March to the NAIC and each state of licence, and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: each subsidiary's blank passes the NAIC edits, carries the actuarial opinion where required, and is filed by its statutory due date with a confirmation.

checklist.step: Bridge statutory results to GAAP and explain every difference
actions: Build the surplus-to-equity and statutory-net-income-to-GAAP bridge by difference type — deferred acquisition costs, non-admitted assets, deferred tax, reserve basis, investment valuation.
Tie the statutory starting point to the filed blank page and line and the GAAP endpoint to the consolidated trial balance.
Have the Controller review each bridging item over the materiality threshold and initial the schedule.
File the bridge with the close package as support for the statutory disclosures in the notes.
checklist.done: a reviewed bridge ties the filed statutory figures to the consolidated GAAP figures with every material difference typed and explained.

checklist.step: Build the Regulation S-X financial statements and schedules
actions: Prepare the balance sheets, statements of operations, comprehensive income, equity and cash flows for the periods Rule 3-02 and Rule 3-04 require, in the Article 7 format for insurance companies.

Prepare the schedules the filing requires — Schedule I summary of investments, Schedule II condensed parent-only financial information, Schedule III supplementary insurance information, Schedule IV reinsurance and Schedule VI supplemental property-casualty information.
Test each schedule's totals back to the audited primary statements and note the tie-out reference on the schedule.
Confirm the parent-only Schedule II is required by testing restricted net assets of subsidiaries against the 25% threshold in Rule 4-08(e).
checklist.done: the S-X statements and every required schedule are prepared in Article 7 form and tie to the primary statements with referenced tie-outs.

checklist.step: Support the PCAOB-registered auditor through the audit
actions: Deliver the prepared-by-client list on the agreed dates and track open items daily with the engagement manager.
Confirm the audit firm's PCAOB registration and its independence confirmation, including that no prohibited non-audit service was provided without Audit Committee pre-approval.
Log every audit adjustment, whether posted or passed, on the summary of uncorrected misstatements and assess it against materiality.
Obtain the signed audit report with the critical audit matters and confirm the opinion date is on or before the filing date.
checklist.done: the audit closes with a signed report from a PCAOB-registered firm, a completed misstatement summary and pre-approved non-audit services.

checklist.step: Present the results to the Audit Committee before filing
actions: Present the financial statements, the significant judgements — reserves, investment valuation, reinsurance recoverability — and the uncorrected misstatement summary.
Have the external auditor present the critical audit matters and any control deficiencies separately from management.
Obtain the committee's approval to file and record it in the minutes with the date.
Confirm the earnings release wording matches the filed statements, with any non-GAAP measure reconciled as Item 10(e) requires.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has approved the statements for filing on a minuted date, with the auditor heard separately.

checklist.step: Tag and file the statements within the deadline
actions: Apply Inline XBRL tagging to the face financials, the notes and the cover page, using standard taxonomy elements and justifying every extension.
Run the EDGAR validation and clear all errors and material warnings before transmission.
Transmit the Form 10-Q within 45 days of quarter end or the Form 10-K within 90 days of fiscal year end and record the accession number.
Distribute the filed statements to Investor Relations and post to the investor site the same day.
checklist.done: the filing is transmitted within its deadline with clean XBRL validation and the accession number recorded.

checklist.step: Retain the close and filing evidence under the retention label
actions: Move the trial balances, signed reconciliations, entry log and support, reserve and valuation memoranda, bridges, schedules and the auditor's report into the repository under the period.
Apply the 7-year retention label and legal hold on anything connected to a restatement, SEC comment or state examination.
Confirm the record is searchable by entity, period, account and accession number.
Give the external auditor and Internal Audit read access to the period folder.
checklist.done: the close and filing evidence is filed under a 7-year label, searchable by entity, period and account, and shared with the auditor.

testing.step: Build the population of accounts, entries, schedules and blanks
actions: Extract the period-end trial balance by entity and the full list of balance sheet accounts requiring reconciliation from the account inventory.
Extract all manual and top-side journal entries posted in the close window with preparer, approver, amount and posting timestamp.
List the Regulation S-X schedules required for the filing and every NAIC blank filed in the year with its submission date.
Record extract dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent populations of accounts, entries, required schedules and filed blanks exist with documented extract parameters.

testing.step: Reconcile the reported statements to the source ledgers
actions: Tie each face financial statement line in the filed document to the consolidated trial balance and the consolidation mapping.
Tie the consolidated trial balance to each entity's source ledger trial balance and explain every elimination.
Confirm the reconciliation account universe covers every balance sheet account in the trial balance with no account excluded silently.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every filed statement line traces to the consolidated and entity trial balances with eliminations explained and the account universe complete.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of high-risk accounts — loss reserves, reinsurance recoverable, investments, deferred acquisition costs, deferred tax — and 100% of top-side entries.
Take 30 reconciliations and 30 manual entries at random using a recorded seed across all entities.
Take 100% of the required S-X schedules and 100% of NAIC blanks filed in the year.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-risk accounts, top-side entries, schedules and blanks is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform sampled reconciliations to independent support
actions: Open each sampled reconciliation and agree the supporting balance to an independent source — custodian statement, reinsurer account, actuarial memorandum, bank statement.
Reject support that is a print of the same ledger balance being reconciled.
Check preparer and reviewer are different people and both signed before the filing date.
Age the open reconciling items and list anything over 60 days without an owner and a clearance date.
testing.done: each sampled reconciliation is agreed to independent support with segregated, pre-filing sign-offs and aged items owned.

testing.step: Test manual and top-side entries to their support
actions: For each sampled entry, open the attached support and re-perform the calculation to the posted amount.
Confirm the approver differs from the preparer and holds delegated authority for the amount.
Scrutinise entries posted after the ledger lock or on the last day of the close for income-statement effect without a subledger source.
Any entry without support, or approved by its preparer, is an exception regardless of amount.
testing.done: each sampled entry is recomputed to its support with segregated approval, and late or unsupported entries are logged.

testing.step: Trace every required S-X schedule into the filed document
actions: Read Rules 5-04 and 7-05 to derive the schedules required, then check each is present in the filed 10-K exhibit or financial statement section.
Recompute the Rule 4-08(e) restricted net assets test to confirm whether Schedule II parent-only information was required, and check its presence against your answer.
Agree each schedule's totals to the audited primary statements and to the notes.
Log any omitted schedule or failed tie-out as an exception with the amount involved.
testing.done: every S-X schedule required by your own reading is present and ties to the audited statements, with omissions logged.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory-to-GAAP bridge and the statutory filings
actions: Agree the bridge's statutory starting figures to the filed blank by page and line for each subsidiary.
Recompute the largest bridging items — non-admitted assets, deferred acquisition costs, deferred tax, reserve basis — from source support.
Confirm the bridge's GAAP endpoint equals the consolidated equity and net income in the filed statements.
Compare each blank's submission date to its statutory due date — 45 days after quarter end, 1 March for the annual — and record any lateness in days.
testing.done: the bridge ties from filed statutory pages to consolidated GAAP, and every blank's timeliness is measured against its statutory due date.

testing.step: Recompute the SEC filing deadlines and check the auditor's report
actions: Derive the 10-Q and 10-K deadlines from the filer status and compare them to the EDGAR acceptance timestamps, recording any overrun in days.
Confirm the audit firm appears on the PCAOB registered firms list at the report date and that the report covers all periods presented.
Check the opinion date is on or before the filing date and that the critical audit matters section is present.
Confirm every non-audit service in the fee table was pre-approved by the Audit Committee before it was performed.
testing.done: filing deadlines are independently recomputed, the auditor's registration and report dating are verified, and non-audit pre-approval is confirmed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the entity, account or schedule, the amount at risk and the reporting consequence.
Assign a root cause from the standing list: interface not confirmed, reconciliation support inadequate, entry approved by preparer, schedule omitted, bridge not tied, or blank filed late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and route any misstatement to the Controller and external auditor for a materiality assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Aggregate the exceptions against the $250,000 escalation threshold and the zero-tolerance schedule and timeliness thresholds.
State the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective and assess whether any exception is a significant deficiency or material weakness.
Confirm the signer prepared or approved no sampled reconciliation, entry or schedule.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the aggregated exception value and any deficiency assessment, with an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the submission calendar and the act of filing — the Form 10-K on EDGAR under Rule 13a-1 and the NAIC and state statutory submissions — with the Controller owning the content and the Corporate Secretary owning the signature and certification pages.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Exchange Act Section 13(a), 15 U.S.C. 78m(a) and Rule 13a-1, 17 CFR 240.13a-1, with Rule 12b-2 filer-status definitions and Rule 12b-25 for extensions, read on eCFR before each annual cycle; NAIC filing dates confirmed against the current Annual Statement Instructions.

In-scope processes.value: External filing execution for the holding company and every insurance subsidiary — filer-status determination, submission calendar maintenance, EDGAR access and codes administration, Inline XBRL validation, transmission and acceptance tracking, and the NAIC and state-of-licence statutory submissions with their confirmations.

In-scope systems.value: Filing assembly, XBRL tagging and EDGAR submission from the financial reporting repository; statutory blanks and state submissions through the NAIC statutory reporting application; the filing calendar and confirmations in the internal regulatory system.

Compliance procedure documented.value: External Filing Procedure — the annual filing calendar by obligation and entity, filer-status computation, EDGAR CIK and CCC custody rules, the pre-transmission validation checklist, the transmission authorisation matrix, and the Rule 12b-25 late-filing escalation path.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel; reviewed annually and whenever filer status changes, a new subsidiary is licensed, or the SEC changes the EDGAR submission requirements.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 10-K within 60, 75 or 90 days after fiscal year end by filer status; Form 10-Q within 45 days of quarter end; NAIC quarterly statements 45 days after quarter end and the annual statement by 1 March to the NAIC and every state of licence; Form 12b-25 by the business day after a missed due date, giving 15 calendar days for a 10-K.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every calendar obligation carries alerts at 30, 14, 7 and 2 days before its due date, and a daily standup from day 75 after fiscal year end until the 10-K is accepted; an unacknowledged alert at 2 days escalates automatically to the CFO.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: EDGAR acceptance messages and accession numbers, the as-filed documents, XBRL validation reports, NAIC and state submission confirmations, filing authorisations and any Form 12b-25, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository indexed by entity and period.
