Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed or late filing, a suspended EDGAR submission, an unfiled state of licence, or a filing transmitted without the authorisation matrix being satisfied is logged as an exception with owner, disposition and Audit Committee reporting date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO authorises every transmission and signs off every late-filing remediation, including the Rule 12b-25 narrative explaining why the report could not be filed within the prescribed time without unreasonable effort or expense.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every filing obligation on the annual calendar for the fiscal year — 10-K, 10-Qs, 8-Ks, proxy, Section 16 forms, NAIC quarterly and annual statements and each state-of-licence submission — for every reporting entity.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any filing accepted after its statutory due date without a valid Rule 12b-25, any obligation on the calendar with no acceptance evidence, or any state of licence missed, is a fail; a suspended EDGAR submission not resolved the same business day is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly and annual; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's filings with an expanded annual pass reconciling the full calendar to the licensed-entity and state-of-licence registers.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Regulatory Reporting and must not have transmitted or authorised any sampled filing.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-timeliness workpaper — calendar completeness reconciliation, acceptance evidence trace, deadline recomputation and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The filing calendar with due dates and acceptance timestamps, EDGAR accession numbers and acceptance messages, NAIC and state confirmations and any Form 12b-25, producible to an SEC comment letter or a state financial examination within 5 business days.

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers NAIC and state insurance department filing queries and resubmits corrected blanks; the Corporate Secretary answers SEC Division of Corporation Finance comments through EDGAR correspondence; the General Counsel clears any late-filing or delinquency communication.

checklist.step: Rebuild the annual filing calendar from the entity and licence registers
actions: List every reporting entity with its CIK for SEC filings and its NAIC company code and states of licence for statutory filings.
Create one calendar row per obligation per entity per period with the regulator, form, due date, preparer, reviewer and authoriser.
Derive statutory due dates from the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and each state's own filing requirement, since some states add supplements.
Have the Controller and the Corporate Secretary confirm the calendar is complete before the year opens.
checklist.done: a confirmed calendar carries one row per obligation per entity per period with named preparer, reviewer, authoriser and due date.

checklist.step: Determine filer status and publish the resulting 10-K deadline
actions: Compute public float at the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter from the closing price and non-affiliate share count.
Apply Rule 12b-2 to set large accelerated (60 days), accelerated (75 days) or non-accelerated (90 days) status and record the calculation.
Update the calendar's 10-K due date to match and reconcile it to the cover-page filer-status boxes.
Notify the Controller, external auditor and Audit Committee chair of any change in status, since it moves the whole close calendar.
checklist.done: filer status is computed from float, the calendar and cover-page boxes agree, and any change is notified to the auditor and Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Keep EDGAR access, codes and Form ID details current
actions: Confirm the CIK, CCC, passphrase and each filer agent's access are valid, and renew EDGAR passwords before their expiry rather than on the filing day.
Maintain current Form ID credentials for every Section 16 filer and add new officers and directors before their first reportable transaction.
Store codes in the password vault with access restricted to the named filing team and log every retrieval.
Test a draft submission on the EDGAR test facility ahead of any new form type.
checklist.done: EDGAR credentials for the registrant and every Section 16 filer are current, vaulted and tested ahead of the filing window.

checklist.step: Run the pre-transmission validation checklist
actions: Check the cover page — period, filer status boxes, shares outstanding as of the latest practicable date, securities registered under Section 12(b) and the well-known seasoned issuer and shell company answers.
Check the exhibit index against the required exhibits, including the certifications, Exhibit 19 insider trading policy and Exhibit 97 clawback policy.
Run Inline XBRL validation and clear every error and material warning, justifying any extension element used.
Confirm the signature page carries the registrant, the principal executive, financial and accounting officers and a majority of the board.
checklist.done: the validation checklist is completed and signed with clean XBRL validation and a complete exhibit index and signature page.

checklist.step: Obtain the documented authorisation to transmit
actions: Confirm the Audit Committee approval to file, the executed Section 302 and 906 certifications and the signed auditor's report are all in the package.
Sign the transmission authorisation naming the document, the period and the intended transmission date.
Withhold authorisation where any sub-certification or reconciliation remains unsigned, and record the reason.
File the authorisation with the submission record.
checklist.done: a signed transmission authorisation naming the document and date is on file before any submission is sent.

checklist.step: Transmit the Form 10-K and confirm acceptance
actions: Transmit through EDGAR on or before the deadline, avoiding the final hour so a suspension can still be corrected the same day.
Watch for the acceptance message and record the accession number and acceptance timestamp on the calendar row.
Where the submission is suspended, read the EDGAR error, correct and retransmit the same business day, and log the event.
Open the filed document on EDGAR and check the rendered document, exhibits and XBRL viewer before declaring the filing closed.
checklist.done: the 10-K shows an EDGAR acceptance timestamp before the deadline, the accession number is logged, and the rendered filing is visually checked.

checklist.step: Transmit the quarterly reports and the current reports on their own clocks
actions: File each Form 10-Q within 45 days of quarter end under Rule 13a-13 and record its acceptance timestamp.
File each Form 8-K within four business days of the triggering event, or on the earlier deadline that applies to Regulation FD and Item 2.02 earnings releases.
File the definitive proxy no later than the date the materials are first sent to security holders.
Reconcile the filings made in the quarter to the calendar rows and close each row with its accession number.
checklist.done: every quarterly, current and proxy filing in the period has an acceptance timestamp inside its own deadline logged against its calendar row.

checklist.step: Submit the NAIC quarterly and annual statements
actions: Submit each subsidiary's quarterly blank to the NAIC within 45 days of quarter end and the annual blank by 1 March, with the jurat page signed by the officers each state requires.
Confirm the NAIC filing receipt for each submission and store the confirmation against the entity and period.
Submit the supporting filings on their own dates — the Management's Discussion and Analysis, the actuarial opinion, the audited statutory statements by 1 June and the risk-based capital report.
Clear any NAIC data-quality query within the response window and refile a corrected blank where required.
checklist.done: every subsidiary blank and supporting filing is submitted by its statutory date with an NAIC confirmation stored against the entity and period.

checklist.step: File with every state of licence and track the confirmations
actions: Take the state-of-licence register per subsidiary and identify which states require a direct filing in addition to the NAIC submission, plus any state supplement or premium tax schedule.
Submit through each state's own portal or the NAIC filing service and capture the confirmation number and date.
Pay any filing fee due and attach the payment reference to the calendar row.
Chase any state that has not acknowledged within its stated window and log the chase.
checklist.done: every state of licence requiring a direct filing has a confirmation number and date recorded against the entity and period.

checklist.step: Monitor the calendar daily through the filing window
actions: Run a daily status call from day 75 after fiscal year end covering every open obligation, its owner and its blockers.
Escalate any obligation without a completed draft at 14 days before its due date to the Controller and the CFO.
Publish a red-amber-green board of all open obligations to the CFO and the Audit Committee chair weekly during the window.
Close each row only on evidence of acceptance, never on a statement that it was sent.
checklist.done: a daily status call and a weekly board run through the filing window, and calendar rows close only on acceptance evidence.

checklist.step: Run the Rule 12b-25 path if a deadline cannot be met
actions: Decide the position at least five business days before the due date, so the notification is a decision rather than a scramble.

File Form 12b-25 no later than one business day after the due date, stating in reasonable detail why the report could not be filed without unreasonable effort or expense, and include the auditor's statement if the reason involves them.
Calendar the filing inside the extension — 15 calendar days for an annual report, 5 for a quarterly — and treat the extended date as immovable.
Notify the exchange, the Audit Committee and Investor Relations, and assess the Form S-3 eligibility and covenant consequences with the General Counsel.
checklist.done: any missed deadline has a Form 12b-25 filed within one business day, the extension date calendared, and the exchange and committee notified.

checklist.step: Handle regulator queries and refilings
actions: Log every SEC comment letter and every NAIC or state data-quality query as an issue with the response due date.
Draft the response with the Controller and the external auditor where the point touches the financial statements, and have the General Counsel clear it.
Where a filing must be amended, file the 10-K/A or a corrected blank and record the new accession or confirmation number against the original row.
Report the query, the response and any refiling to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: every regulator query has a logged issue, a cleared response inside the due date, and any refiling linked to the original filing record.

checklist.step: Reconcile the year's filings to the obligation register
actions: At year end, compare the closed calendar rows to the obligation register derived from the entity and licence lists.
Investigate any obligation with no closed row and any closed row with no acceptance evidence.
Confirm entities licensed or surrendered during the year had their obligations added or ended on the correct dates.
Publish the annual filing compliance summary with counts filed on time, filed late and missed.
checklist.done: the year's closed rows reconcile to the obligation register and an annual summary reports on-time, late and missed counts.

checklist.step: Report filing performance to the Audit Committee
actions: Present the on-time filing rate, every late filing with its cause, and the status of any regulator query or refiling.
Name the owner and the fix for each late filing rather than reporting the count alone.
Record the committee's directions as tracked actions with owners and dates.
Load the pack into the board portal and record the minutes reference.
checklist.done: filing performance with named causes and owners is minuted at the Audit Committee with tracked actions.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence under the retention label
actions: Move the EDGAR acceptance messages, as-filed documents, XBRL validation reports, NAIC and state confirmations, authorisations and any Form 12b-25 into the repository under the entity and period.
Apply the 7-year retention label and legal hold on anything connected to an open comment letter, examination or restatement.
Confirm the record is searchable by entity, period, form type and accession or confirmation number.
Give Internal Audit read access ahead of the quarterly test.
checklist.done: all acceptance and confirmation evidence is filed under a 7-year label and searchable by entity, form type and accession number.

testing.step: Build the population of filing obligations for the period
actions: Derive the obligation list independently from the legal entity register, the SEC registration record and each subsidiary's state-of-licence schedule, rather than from the maintained calendar.
Add the event-driven obligations by reading the year's board minutes, press releases and material contracts for 8-K triggers.
Extract the maintained calendar with its closed rows and acceptance references for comparison.
Record extract dates, sources and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation population, including event-driven 8-K triggers, exists alongside the maintained calendar.

testing.step: Reconcile the derived obligations to the maintained calendar
actions: Match each derived obligation to a calendar row and list obligations absent from the calendar — these are the dangerous ones.
List calendar rows with no derived obligation and confirm they are genuine rather than duplicates.
Check states of licence added or surrendered in the year against the obligations opened or closed on the matching dates.
Sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every derived obligation ties to a calendar row, with omissions listed and licence changes reflected on the correct dates.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of periodic SEC filings — the 10-K, each 10-Q and the proxy — and 100% of NAIC annual statements.
Take 100% of 8-Ks filed and all derived 8-K triggers to test for filings that should have been made.
Take 25 state-of-licence submissions at random using a recorded seed across subsidiaries.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all periodic filings, all 8-K triggers and a state-submission sample is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the filer-status and deadline computation
actions: Recompute public float from the closing price and non-affiliate share count at the last business day of the second fiscal quarter, using the share register and the affiliate list.
Derive the filer status and the 60, 75 or 90-day 10-K deadline and the 40 or 45-day 10-Q deadline independently.
Compare your deadlines to the calendar's and to the cover-page boxes on the filed documents.
Any status overstatement that bought extra days is a reportable failure, not a computation difference.
testing.done: filer status and every periodic deadline are independently recomputed and agreed to the calendar and the filed cover pages.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to its acceptance evidence
actions: Open the EDGAR filing index for the registrant's CIK and locate each sampled filing with its accession number and acceptance timestamp.
Compare the acceptance timestamp — not the submission attempt — to the recomputed deadline and record any overrun in hours.
For statutory filings, open the NAIC receipt and the state portal confirmation and compare the date to the statutory due date.
List any calendar row closed with no acceptance evidence behind it as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled filing has an acceptance timestamp or confirmation compared against its recomputed deadline, with unevidenced closures logged.

testing.step: Test for filings that should have been made and were not
actions: Read the year's board and committee minutes, material contracts, executive changes, restatement decisions and material cyber incidents against the Form 8-K item list.
For each identified trigger, locate the filed 8-K and compare the filing date to the four-business-day limit.
For any trigger with no filing, obtain the documented conclusion that no item applied and judge it independently.
Treat an undocumented no-file conclusion as an exception.
testing.done: every identified 8-K trigger has a timely filing or an independently judged, documented no-file conclusion.

testing.step: Test the authorisation and validation controls before transmission
actions: For each sampled periodic filing, open the signed transmission authorisation and confirm it pre-dates the transmission timestamp.
Confirm the completed validation checklist, the XBRL validation report and the signature page were all in the package before authorisation.
Check that transmission was performed by a person on the authorisation matrix and not the same person who authorised it, where the matrix requires separation.
Review any suspended submission and confirm it was corrected and retransmitted the same business day.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a pre-dated authorisation, a completed validation package and a matrix-compliant transmitter.

testing.step: Recompute the Rule 12b-25 mechanics where used
actions: For each Form 12b-25 filed, compare its filing date to one business day after the missed due date.
Recompute the extension end date — 15 calendar days for an annual report, 5 for a quarterly — and compare it to the eventual filing acceptance timestamp.
Read the stated reason and judge whether it supports the 'without unreasonable effort or expense' standard rather than restating the delay.
Confirm the auditor's statement was included where the reason involved the audit.
testing.done: every Form 12b-25 is timing-tested against the one-business-day and extension limits with its stated reason judged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the entity, obligation, regulator, days late and the consequence — delinquency, Form S-3 ineligibility, exchange notice or state penalty.

Assign a root cause from the standing list: obligation missing from the calendar, content late from the close, credentials expired, submission suspended, trigger not identified, or state filing overlooked.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and route any missed filing to the General Counsel for a delinquency assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and state the conclusion as effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Confirm the signer transmitted and authorised none of the sampled filings.
Report the conclusion, every late or missed filing and any delinquency consequence to the Audit Committee at its next meeting.
File the signed workpaper with its evidence references in the compliance evidence repository under the period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and on-time rate, with every late filing reported to the Audit Committee on a recorded date.
